D32.title: Conjectural Eisenstein subspaces in degree-five cohomology of \(\Gamma_0(p)\)
D32.statement: Fix a prime $p$. Let $\Gamma_0(p)\subset SL(4,\mathbb Z)$ be the congruence subgroup in the paper, and let $d_f$ and $d_\eta$ denote the degrees of the fields generated by the Hecke eigenvalues of a holomorphic newform $f$ and a cuspidal cohomology eigenclass $\eta$, respectively. Let $\sigma_2$ and $\sigma_4$ be the Galois representations attached to weight $2$ and weight $4$ holomorphic newforms, and let $\tau$ be the conjecturally attached Galois representation for a pair of nonselfdual cuspidal classes $\eta,\eta'\in H^3(\Gamma_0^*(p),\mathbb C)$. **Conjectural Eisenstein-subspace statement.** The group $H^5(\Gamma_0(p),\mathbb C)$ contains the following Eisenstein subspaces: for every weight $2$ newform of level $p$, two $d_f$-dimensional subspaces attached to $\mathrm{IIa}(\sigma_2)$ and $\mathrm{IIb}(\sigma_2)$; for every weight $4$ newform of level $p$ whose functional-equation sign $w$ is negative, one $d_f$-dimensional subspace attached to $\mathrm{IV}(\sigma_2)$; and for every pair of nonselfdual classes $\eta,\eta'$, two $d_\eta$-dimensional subspaces attached to $\mathrm{IIIa}(\tau)$ and $\mathrm{IIIb}(\tau)$. These assertions describe the conjectural Eisenstein contribution to degree-five cohomology; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

D32.title: Strict endoscopic conjecture for Siegel modular forms of level 2
D32.statement:
Let $\mathbb V_{l,m}$ be the local system on $\mathcal A_2[2]$ indexed by $(l,m)$, and write

$$
k=l+m+4,\qquad k'=l-m+2.
$$

Let $S[\Gamma_0(4),k']$ denote the motive-valued contribution associated with elliptic cusp forms of weight $k'$ and level $\Gamma_0(4)$, and let $e_{\rm End^s}(\mathcal A_2[2],\mathbb V_{l,m})$ denote the strict endoscopic part of the inner cohomology. **Strict endoscopic conjecture.** The strict endoscopic part is

$$
e_{\rm End^s}(\mathcal A_2[2],\mathbb V_{l,m})=-5L^{m+1}\cdot \dim S_k(\Gamma_0(4))\cdot S[\Gamma_0(4),k'],
$$

where $S[\Gamma_0(4),2]$ is interpreted as $-L-1$. This predicts that the strict endoscopic cohomology is described by elliptic modular forms, subject to the stated exceptional interpretation at weight $2$.

D32.title: Yoshida-type lifting conjecture for level 2 and level 4 elliptic forms
D32.statement:
Let $S_{j,k}(\Gamma_2[2])$ be the space of Siegel cusp forms of weight $(j,k)$ on the principal level-$2$ subgroup, and let $w_2$ act on newforms of level $2$. For new eigenforms

$$
f\in S_{l+m+4}(\Gamma_0(2))^{\rm new},\qquad g\in S_{l-m+2}(\Gamma_0(2))^{\rm new},
$$

write $L(f,s)$ and $L(g,s)$ for their $L$-functions. **Yoshida-type lifting conjecture.** There is a Siegel Hecke eigenform $F\in S_{l-m,m+3}(\Gamma_2[2])$ with

$$
L(F,s)=L(f,s)L(g,s-m-1).
$$

It occurs with multiplicity $5$ when $f$ and $g$ have the same $w_2$-eigenvalue and with multiplicity $1$ when their eigenvalues are opposite. Likewise, for new eigenforms at level $4$,

$$
f\in S_{l+m+4}(\Gamma_0(4))^{\rm new},\qquad g\in S_{l-m+2}(\Gamma_0(4))^{\rm new},
$$

there is such an $F$ with the same spinor $L$-function, occurring with multiplicity $5$. This proposes a level-$2$ analogue of Yoshida lifting and explains predicted endoscopic pieces of the cohomology.

D32.title: Expanded endoscopic conjecture for equal weights at level 2
D32.statement:
Let $\mathbb V_{m,m}$ be the equal-weight local system on $\mathcal A_2[2]$, set $k=2m+4$, and write $\tau_{N,k}=\dim S_k(\Gamma_0(N))^{\rm new}$ and $\tau_k^\pm=\dim S_k^\pm(\Gamma_0(2))^{\rm new}$. Let $s[\lambda]$ denote the irreducible $\mathbb S_6$-representation indexed by $\lambda$. **Equal-weight expanded endoscopic conjecture.** The expanded endoscopic part is

$$
L^{m+1}(L+1)\begin{cases}
\tau_k^+s[1^6]+\tau_{4,k}s[3^2]+\tau_k^-s[5,1],&m\text{ odd},\\
(\tau_k^-+\tau_{1,k})s[2^3]+(\tau_k^++\tau_{1,k})s[4,2]+\tau_{1,k}s[6],&m\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
$$

This is the equal-weight counterpart of the expanded endoscopic prediction and accounts for the parity-dependent Saito–Kurokawa contributions.

D32.title: Maulik–Pandharipande quasi-modularity conjecture for reduced K3 descendents
D32.statement: Let $S$ be an elliptically fibered $K3$ surface with section, with section and fiber classes $\mathbf{s},\mathbf{f}\in H^2(S,\mathbb{Z})$ spanning $\operatorname{Pic}(S)$. For $g\geq0$ and $m\geq1$, let ${\mathsf{F}}^S_{g,m}(\tau_{k_1}(\gamma_{l_1})\cdots\tau_{k_r}(\gamma_{l_r}))$ be the reduced descendent potential defined by summing over classes $m\mathbf{s}+n\mathbf{f}$. **Maulik–Pandharipande quasi-modularity conjecture.** This potential is the Fourier expansion in $q$ of a quasi-modular form of level $m^2$ with pole at $q=0$ of order at most $m^2$. This conjecture concerns the modular structure of reduced Gromov–Witten theory of $K3$ surfaces; the source gives no resolution status.

D32.title: The weak stability conjecture for level mapping class groups
D32.statement:
Let $\Sigma_g$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g$, let $\operatorname{Mod}_g(L)$ be the level-$L$ mapping class group, and let $\gamma$ be a simple closed nonseparating curve on $\Sigma_g$. Write $(\operatorname{Mod}_g(L))_\gamma$ for the stabilizer of $\gamma$ in $\operatorname{Mod}_g(L)$. For fixed $L \geq 2$ and $k \geq 1$, consider the natural map

$$
\operatorname{H}_k((\operatorname{Mod}_g(L))_\gamma;{\mathbb{Q}}) \longrightarrow \operatorname{H}_k(\operatorname{Mod}_g(L);{\mathbb{Q}}).
$$

**Stability conjecture.** For fixed $L \geq 2$ and $k \geq 1$, there exists some $N$ such that if $g \geq N$ and $\gamma$ is a simple closed nonseparating curve on $\Sigma_g$, then this map is a surjection.

This weaker stability statement is presented as sufficient for the isomorphism conjecture, extending the degree-two homological argument to higher degrees. Its general validity is not established in the source.

D32.title: The converse of the WLP criterion for level monomial ideals
D32.statement: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $R=K[x,y,z]$, and let $I_{alpha,beta,gamma,t}$ denote the level monomial almost complete intersection used in the preceding criterion. The criterion gives three cases ensuring failure or presence of the WLP. **Converse conjecture.** If $R/I_{alpha,beta,gamma,t}$ fails to have the WLP, then one of cases (1), (2), or (3) holds. This converse is intended to complete the characterization of level monomial ideals in three variables that fail to have the WLP; the supplied text does not state its resolution.

D32.title: Paulin's geometric level raising conjecture for the eigencurve
D32.statement:
Fix distinct primes $p$ and $l$, and an integer $N$ coprime to $pl$. Let $\mathcal{E}$ be the cuspidal eigencurve of tame level $\Gamma_0(Nl)$, parametrising overconvergent cuspidal $p$-adic modular eigenforms. For a point $\phi$ of $\mathcal{E}$ corresponding to an eigenform $f_\phi$, let $\pi_{f_\phi,l}$ be the associated representation of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_l)$. An irreducible connected component $\mathcal{Z}$ of $\mathcal{E}$ is **generically unramified principal series** if the representations associated to its points away from a discrete set are unramified principal series, and **generically special** if they are special away from a discrete set. Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of

$$
X^2-t_lX+ls_l,
$$

where $t_l$ and $s_l$ are the $T_l$ and $S_l$ eigenvalues of $f_\phi$. **Paulin's geometric level raising conjecture.** If $\mathcal{Z}$ is generically unramified principal series and there is a point $\phi$ on $\mathcal{Z}$ where the ratio of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ is $l^{\pm 1}$ and $\pi_{f_\phi,l}$ is special, then there exists a generically special component $\mathcal{Z'}$ intersecting $\mathcal{Z}$ at $\phi$. This predicts that a special representation at a level-raising point lies on a component whose generic local representation is special, extending geometric level raising phenomena on the eigencurve beyond the cases established by the paper's theorem.

D32.title: Storage-efficiency conjecture for load-balancing modulation codes
D32.statement:
Let $l$ be the number of choices in the load-balancing modulation code, let $q$ be the number of charge levels, let $n$ be the number of memory cells, and let $k$ denote the message-length parameter. The storage efficiency is denoted by $\gamma$.

**Storage-efficiency conjecture.** If $l=2$ and $q-1=c\ln n$, then the load-balancing modulation code has storage efficiency $\gamma=k$ with probability $1-o(1)$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$. If $q-1=c$, the storage efficiency is

$$
\gamma=\frac{c\ln 2}{\ln\ln n}k
$$

with probability $1-o(1)$.

The conjecture asserts that the ball-loading performance of this modulation code matches that of the random-loading algorithm with two random choices. The supplied source gives no resolution status, so it is recorded as open.

D32.title: Jacobian parametrization conjecture for the generalized ultradiscrete Toda isolevel set
D32.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be the tropical spectral curve associated with $\operatorname{\mathcal{T}}(M,N)$, let $J(\Gamma)$ denote its Jacobian, and let $\Phi^{-1}(\xi)$ denote the corresponding isolevel set. **Jacobian parametrization conjecture.** The theta-functional solution described above induces an isomorphism

$$
J(\Gamma)^{\oplus M!}\cong\Phi^{-1}(\xi).
$$

This asserts that the isolevel set is completely parametrized by $M!$ copies of the tropical Jacobian through the preceding family of solutions.

D32.title: Gabrielov's regular triangulation conjecture for definable functions
D32.statement:
Let $K
e\varnothing$ be a compact definable set in ${\mathbb R}^m$, and let $f:K\to{\mathbb R}$ be a definable function. Write the graph over an open simplex $\Delta$ as

$$
\Gamma=\{(\mathbf{x},t)\mid \mathbf{x}\in\Delta,\ t=f(\mathbf{x})\}.
$$

A **regular $n$-cell** is understood as in the source's Definition 1.1. A definable triangulation of $K$ is a triangulation whose simplices are definable.

**Gabrielov's regular triangulation conjecture.** There exists a definable triangulation of $K$ such that, for each $n\leq\dim K$ and every open $n$-simplex $\Delta$ of the triangulation, $\Gamma$ is a regular $n$-cell, and either $f$ is constant on $\Delta$ or every nonempty level set

$$
\Gamma\cap\{t=c\}
$$

is a regular $(n-1)$-cell.

This conjecture is presented as a key step in Gabrielov's triangulation program: a compatible triangulation of increasing definable families of compact sets would imply the homotopy equivalence conjecture above. The source does not provide a resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

D32.title: Kowalski–Michel–VanderKam mass equidistribution conjecture in the level aspect
D32.statement: Let $f$ be a classical holomorphic newform of fixed weight $k$ and level $q$, with mass $d\nu_f=|f(z)|^2y^{k-2}\,dx\,dy$ on $Y_0(q)=\Gamma_0(q)\backslash\mathbb H$. Let $\pi_q:Y_0(q)\rightarrow Y_0(1)$ be the canonical projection, and let $\mu$ denote the Poincaré measure on $Y_0(1)$. **Kowalski–Michel–VanderKam's mass equidistribution conjecture.** If $f$ traverses a sequence of newforms of fixed weight and increasing level $q\rightarrow\infty$, then the pushforward $\mu_f:=\pi_{q*}(\nu_f)$ equidistributes with respect to $\mu$. This is the level-aspect analogue of the Rudnick–Sarnak quantum unique ergodicity conjecture, reversing the roles of weight and level; the supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

D32.title: Etingof's conjecture on the graded pieces of rational double affine Hecke algebra representations
D32.statement:
Let $\Gamma_n$ be the object whose $(i,j)$-graded piece is denoted by ${\rm{gr}}_{i,j}(\Gamma_n)$. Fix a rational parameter $h$ with denominator $m>1$, let $\tilde{\mathfrak a}=\tilde{\mathfrak a}_\Lambda$ be the Lie subalgebra defined by the level-$1$ weight $\Lambda$, and let $P^{\tilde{\mathfrak a}}_+$ be its set of dominant integral weights. For $\mu\in P^{\tilde{\mathfrak a}}_+$, write $V^{\tilde{\mathfrak a}}_\mu$ for the corresponding irreducible integrable module, and let $V^{\tilde{\mathfrak a}}_\mu[\omega_0-n\delta,j]$ denote the subspace of weight $\omega_0-n\delta$ on which the $m$-th Casimir operator has eigenvalue $j$. **Etingof's conjecture.** There exists an isomorphism of $\mathbb{C}$-vector spaces

$$
{\rm{gr}}_{i,j}(\Gamma_n)=\bigoplus_\mu V^{\tilde{\mathfrak a}}_\mu[\omega_0-n\delta,j]\otimes {\rm{Hom}}_{\tilde{\mathfrak a}}(V^{\tilde{\mathfrak a}}_\mu,V_{\omega_0}^{\widetilde{\mathfrak{g}\mathfrak{l}}_\ell}),
$$

where the sum is over all weights $\mu\in P^{\tilde{\mathfrak a}}_+$ such that $\langle\mu,\mu\rangle=-2i$. This conjecture predicts a representation-theoretic description of the bigraded pieces associated with the rational double affine Hecke algebra, relating them to modules for the subalgebra $\tilde{\mathfrak a}$.

D32.title: Nonvanishing of the cusp differential in cohomology of Bianchi groups
D32.statement:
Let $\Gamma_s$ be the stabilizer of a singular cusp $s$, let $M$ be a coefficient module as above, and let $d_2^{0,1}$ be the differential in the spectral sequence computing $H^2(\Gamma,M)$. The restriction of this differential to the summand associated with $s$ is a map

$$
H^1(\Gamma_s,M)\longrightarrow E_2^{2,0}.
$$

**Nonvanishing conjecture.** This restricted differential is nonzero.

This nonvanishing would determine the contribution of singular cusps to the computation of $H^2(\Gamma,M)$ by showing that the corresponding $E_2^{0,1}$ contribution is not killed trivially. The source reports considerable computational evidence, but does not establish the claim in general.

D32.title: Adem–Ge–Pan–Petrosyan collapse conjecture for semidirect products
D32.statement:
Let $G\cong \mathbb{Z}/m$ be a finite cyclic group, let $L\cong\mathbb{Z}^n$ be a finitely generated free abelian group, let $\rho\colon G\to\operatorname{aut}_{\mathbb{Z}}(L)$ be a group homomorphism, and set $\Gamma=L\rtimes_{\rho}G$. The Lyndon–Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence associated to the semidirect product $L\rtimes_{\rho}G$ has terms arising from the extension $1\to L\to\Gamma\to G\to 1$. **Adem–Ge–Pan–Petrosyan conjecture.** The spectral sequence collapses in the strongest sense: all differentials in the $E_r$-term for $r\geq 2$ are trivial and all extension problems at the $E_{\infty}$-level are trivial. In particular, for all $k\geq 0$, 

$$
H^k(\Gamma;\mathbb{Z})\cong\bigoplus_{i+j=k}H^i(G;H^j(L)).
$$

The paper proves the conjecture when the $G$-action on $L$ is free outside the origin, but gives an example with $n=6$ and $m=4$ in which the second differential does not vanish; thus the conjecture is false in general.

D32.title: Ferromagnetic ordering of energy levels for symmetric spin chains
D32.statement:
Consider a chain of $L$ urns, each containing $n$ balls, with the exchange dynamics described above: at each bond $\\{x,x+1\\}$, a random number of balls is selected according to $\rho_{x,x+1}$ and exchanged uniformly between the neighboring urns. The dynamics preserves the total number of red balls. For $1\leq k\leq nL-1$, let $\gamma_k$ denote the spectral gap restricted to configurations with exactly $k$ red balls and $nL-k$ white balls.

**Ferromagnetic ordering conjecture.** The spectral gap $\gamma_k$ is independent of $k$; equivalently,

$$
\gamma_k=\gamma_1,
$$

where $\gamma_1$ is the spectral gap of the associated random walk.

This is an analogue of Aldous's spectral-gap conjecture for the symmetric exclusion process and reflects the hidden $\operatorname{SU}(2)$ symmetry of the symmetric urn-mixing dynamics. The cases $k=0$ and $k=nL$ are excluded because the corresponding state spaces contain only one configuration and hence have no spectral gap.

D32.title: The weak Lefschetz property conjecture for level monomial ideals
D32.statement:
Let $R$ be the polynomial ring in the variables used to define the ideal, over a field $K$ of characteristic zero. Let $0<\alpha\leq\beta\leq\gamma\leq2(\alpha+\beta)$, let $t\geq\frac{1}{3}(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)$, and assume that $\alpha+\beta+\gamma$ is divisible by three. Exclude $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,t)=(2,9,13,9)$ and $(3,7,14,9)$. **The weak Lefschetz property conjecture.** The algebra

$$
R/I_{\alpha+t,\beta+t,\gamma+t,\alpha,\beta,\gamma}
$$

fails to have the weak Lefschetz property if and only if $t$ is even, $\alpha+\beta+\gamma$ is odd, and $\alpha=\beta$ or $\beta=\gamma$. The conjecture gives an explicit characteristic-zero criterion for failure of the weak Lefschetz property in this family; the two exceptional parameter tuples are excluded, and no resolution is supplied here.

D32.title: Ratios Conjecture prediction for the 1-level density of Dirichlet L-functions
D32.statement:
Let $q$ be a modulus, let $f$ be the test function used in the 1-level density, and let $D_{1;q}(\widehat{f})$ denote the corresponding density with scaling parameter $Q=q$. Write $gamma$ for Euler's constant and let the sum over $p\mid q$ run over primes dividing $q$. **Ratios Conjecture's prediction.** The 1-level density equals

$$
D_{1;q}(\widehat{f})=f(0)\left(1-\frac{\log(8\pi e^{\gamma})}{\log q}-\frac{\sum_{p\mid q}\frac{\log p}{p-1}}{\log q}\right)+\int_0^{\infty}\frac{f(0)-f(t)}{q^{t/2}-q^{-t/2}}\,dt+O_{\epsilon}\left(q^{-\frac12+\epsilon}\right).
$$

This is the lower-order prediction obtained by extending the Ratios Conjecture to general moduli; the paper compares its proven density calculations with this formula where both are available.

D32.title: Definable triangulation conjecture for functions on compact definable sets
D32.statement:
Let $f:K\to\mathbb{R}$ be a definable function on a compact definable set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^m$. A **definable triangulation** of $K$ is a definable triangulation whose open simplices satisfy the following conditions. For each $n\leq\dim K$ and each open $n$-simplex $\Delta$ of the triangulation, let

$$
\Gamma=\{(\mathbf{x},t)\mid \mathbf{x}\in\Delta,\ t=f(\mathbf{x})\}
$$

be the graph of the restriction of $f$ to $\Delta$. **Definable triangulation conjecture.** There exists a definable triangulation of $K$ such that $\Gamma$ is a topologically regular $n$-cell, and either $f$ is constant on $\Delta$ or every nonempty level set

$$
\Gamma\cap\{t=\text{constant}\}
$$

is a topologically regular $(n-1)$-cell. This conjecture was proposed as motivation for studying semi-monotone sets, monotone functions, and monotone maps; the paper develops those theories and proves related regular-cell results, but the supplied text does not state whether this triangulation conjecture itself is resolved.

D32.title: Böcherer's paramodular conjecture for prime-level eigenforms
D32.statement:
Let $p$) be prime and let $F\in S^k(\Gamma^{\mathrm{para}}[p])^+$ be a paramodular Hecke eigenform of even weight $k$. For each fundamental discriminant $D<0$, let $A_F(D)$ denote the normalized average of the Fourier coefficients of $F$ indexed by quadratic forms of discriminant $D$, and let $\chi_D$ be the associated quadratic character. Put $\alpha_D=1+\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)$. **Böcherer's conjecture.**

$$
A_F(D)^2=\alpha_D C_F L(F,1/2,\chi_D)|D|^{k-1},
$$

where $C_F$ is a nonnegative constant depending only on $F$. If $F$ is a Gritsenko lift, then $C_F>0$; if $F$ is not a lift, then $C_F=0$ if and only if $L(F,1/2)=0$. This is the paramodular analogue of Böcherer's conjecture relating quadratic-twist central values to averages of Fourier coefficients; it is proved for lifts and supported numerically for nonlifts.

D32.title: Twisted Böcherer conjecture for squarefree-level paramodular forms
D32.statement:
Let $N$ be squarefree, and let $F\in S^k(\Gamma^{\mathrm{para}}[N])$ be a Hecke eigenform that is not a Gritsenko lift. For fundamental discriminants $\ell$ and $D$ with $\ell D<0$, let $B_{\ell,F}(D)$ be the twisted average of Fourier coefficients indexed by quadratic forms of discriminant $D$. If $\Delta_0$ is the fundamental discriminant associated to $\Delta$, define

$$
\alpha_\Delta=\prod_{p\mid N}\left(1+\left(\frac{\Delta_0}{p}\right)\right).
$$

**Twisted Böcherer conjecture.**

$$
B_{\ell,F}(D)^2=\alpha_{\ell D}C_{\ell,F}L(F,1/2,\chi_D)|D|^{k-1},
$$

where $C_{\ell,F}$ is independent of $D$, and $C_{\ell,F}=0$ if and only if $L(F,1/2,\ell)=0$. This generalizes the prime-level paramodular form of Böcherer's conjecture by allowing an auxiliary discriminant and arbitrary squarefree level; the notation and conjectural relation are presented as the basis for numerical tests on nonlifts.

D32.title: Multiplicity one for Siegel cusp forms of degree 2 and full level
D32.statement:
Let $S_k(\Gamma_2)$ be the space of holomorphic Siegel cusp forms of weight $k$ for $\Gamma_2=\operatorname{Sp}_4(\mathbb{Z})$. Let $f_1,f_2\in S_k(\Gamma_2)$ be Hecke eigenforms, and write $\lambda_{p^r}(f_i)$ for their Hecke eigenvalues. **Multiplicity-one conjecture.** If, for every prime $p$, 

$$
\lambda_p(f_1)=\lambda_p(f_2)\quad\text{and}\quad\lambda_{p^2}(f_1)=\lambda_{p^2}(f_2),
$$

then there exists a constant $c$ such that $f_1=cf_2$. This is the degree-two, full-level analogue of multiplicity one for ${\rm GL}_2$ and remains unknown for cuspidal representations on ${\rm GSp}_4$.

D32.title: Uniform distortion conjecture for simplicial power maps
D32.statement:
Let $T=\triangle(,0,)$ be a triangle and denote its angle at $0$ by $\theta=\measuredangle(\xi,0,\eta)$. Let $T^q$ be the $q$th level of the regular 1-4 subdivision of $T$. For $\gamma>0$, define the power map $h(z)=z^\gamma$, and assume that $\gamma\theta<\pi$. **Uniform distortion conjecture.** The simplicial maps $h^q$, obtained by sampling $h$ at the vertices of $T^q$ and extending by linearity, are homeomorphisms satisfying

$$
\mathrm{\textbf{D}}(h^q)\leq K
$$

for some $K\geq 1$ independent of $q$. This conjecture concerns uniform quasiconformal control of simplicial approximations to power maps; the stated claim is not accompanied by a resolution in the supplied text.

D32.title: Integral generators conjecture for square-free moonshine groups
D32.statement: Let $N$ be square-free, let $g>0$ be the genus of the moonshine modular curve associated to the group $\Gamma_0(N)^+$, and consider its function field. **Integral generators conjecture.** This function field admits two generators whose $q$-expansions have integer coefficients after the lead coefficient has been normalized to equal one, and the orders of their poles at $i\infty$ are at most $g+2$. This conjecture extends the authors' results on integral $q$-expansions and small pole orders to all square-free levels, independently of the gap sequence at $i\infty$; the genus-one case follows from known results, while the genus-two and genus-three cases were analyzed separately in the paper.

D32.title: Existence of generalized Macmahon modules by analytic continuation
D32.statement: Fix non-negative integers $l_1,\dots,l_t,l'_1,\dots,l'_t$, and for sufficiently large $k$ let $L_k=(l_1,\dots,l_t,0,\dots,0,l'_t,\dots,l'_1)$ be the vector with $k$ components. Let $\mathcal N_{\gamma(L_k),\beta}^{(p)}(u)$ be the corresponding module for the quantum toroidal algebra $\mathcal E_n$. **Existence conjecture for generalized Macmahon modules.** There exists a lowest weight admissible tame $\mathcal E_n$-module $\mathcal M_{\gamma(l),\beta}^{(n;p),\gamma(l')}(u,K)$ of level $K$ that is the analytic continuation of $\mathcal N_{\gamma(L_k),\beta}^{(p)}(u)$ with respect to $k$. This conjecture extends the Macmahon-module construction; the source does not state a resolution.

D32.title: Sufficiency of level raising for 1⊕χ_l^{k−1}
D32.statement:
Let $\rho:\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})\to\operatorname{GL}_2(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_l)$ be the odd semisimple representation $\mathbf{1}\oplus\chi_l^{k-1}$, with $k\geq4$ even. Let $N$ be squarefree and coprime to $l$, and suppose that $\rho$ arises from a weight-$k$ newform in $\mathcal{S}_k(\Gamma_0(N))$. For a prime $p\nmid Nl$, the level-raising condition is

$$
(p^k-1)(p^{k-2}-1)\equiv0\pmod l.
$$

**Level-raising sufficiency conjecture.** If this condition holds at $p$, then $\rho$ arises from a weight-$k$ newform in $\mathcal{S}_k(\Gamma_0(Np))$. This is the precise conjecture proposed in the paper and is open there.

D32.title: Exact-level-set criterion for Solyanik failure in convex density bases
D32.statement:
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a homothecy invariant density basis of convex sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$. Suppose that for some $\gamma>1$, for every $0<\alpha<1$ there is a set $E_{\alpha,\gamma}$ such that

$$
\left|\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:M_{\mathcal{B}}\chi_{E_{\alpha,\gamma}}(x)>\alpha\right\}\right|\geq\gamma|E_{\alpha,\gamma}|.
$$

**Exact-level-set criterion.** Then there exist a set $E_\gamma$ and a constant $c(\gamma)>1$ such that

$$
\left|\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:M_{\mathcal{B}}\chi_{E_\gamma}(x)=1\right\}\right|\geq c(\gamma)|E_\gamma|.
$$

This is presented as a sufficient criterion for proving the preceding Solyanik conjecture: it would reduce persistent failure of the limit to the existence of a set whose maximal function equals one on a quantitatively larger set. The supplied text does not prove this criterion.

D32.title: Universality conjecture for low-lying zeros of automorphic families
D32.statement: Let $\mathfrak{F}$ be a rank $0$ essentially homogeneous family. Write the zeros of each completed $L$-function as $\frac12+i\gamma_j^{(\pi)}$ and normalize them by $\widetilde{\gamma}_j^{(\pi)}=\gamma_j^{(\pi)}\log C(\pi)/(2\pi)$. Let $W_0^{(r)}$, $W_-^{(r)}$, and $W_+^{(r)}$ denote the fluctuation $r$-level densities associated with the four limiting random-matrix symmetry types. **Universality conjecture.** The low-lying zeros follow the table: non-self-dual families have type $\mathrm{U}(\infty)$ and density $W_0^{(r)}$; orthogonal families have type $\operatorname{Sp}(\infty)$ and density $W_-^{(r)}$; symplectic families with $\varepsilon=1$ have type $\operatorname{SO}_{\mathrm{even}}(\infty)$ and density $W_+^{(r)}$; and symplectic families with $\varepsilon=-1$ have type $\operatorname{SO}_{\mathrm{odd}}(\infty)$ and density $W_-^{(r)}$, in each case for $r\geq 1$. This is the low-lying-zero form of the expected Katz–Sarnak universality law; the source does not state a general proof.

D32.title: Stability conjecture for distinguishing newforms at squarefree level
D32.statement: Let $n_0(N,k)$ be the smallest nonnegative integer such that, for any newforms $f,g\in S_k(\Gamma_0(N))$, equality $a_n(f)=a_n(g)$ for all $n\leq n_0(N,k)$ implies $f=g$. Let $N\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ be squarefree. **Stability conjecture.** There exists $K\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ such that if $k\geq K$ is an even integer, then $n_0(N,k)$ is equal to the least prime that does not divide $N$. This predicts that, for fixed squarefree level, the number of initial Fourier coefficients needed to distinguish newforms eventually stabilizes at the first prime not dividing the level.

D32.title: Irreducibility conjecture for reductions at the boundary of weight space
D32.statement:
Let $f$ be a newform of weight $k\geq 2$ and level $\Gamma_1(Np^r)$, where $r\geq 2$, whose character has $p$-part $\chi$ of conductor $p^r$, and let $\alpha$ be its $U_p$-eigenvalue. Let $V_{k,\alpha,\chi}$ be the associated local Galois representation and let $\overline{V}_{k,\alpha,\chi}$ be the semisimplification of its mod-$p$ reduction. Normalize the valuation $v_\chi$ so that its image on ${\mathbb{Q}}_p(\chi)^\times$ is ${\mathbb{Z}}$.

**Boundary irreducibility conjecture.** If $v_\chi(\alpha)\notin{\mathbb{Z}}$, then $\overline{V}_{k,\alpha,\chi}$ is irreducible.

This local assertion is proposed to explain patterns in the slopes of forms near the boundary of weight space. The source notes that several global results instead force integral slopes in particular levels, but does not resolve the general conjecture.

D32.title: Spectral multiplicity conjecture for Maaß newforms
D32.statement: Let $q$ be an odd positive integer, and let $s(q)$ denote the number of distinct odd primes $p$ for which $p^2$ divides $q$. Consider the new part of the discrete spectrum of the Laplacian on $\Gamma_0(q)\backslash\mathbb{H}$. **Spectral multiplicity conjecture.** The multiplicity of an eigenvalue $\lambda>1/4$ is bounded above by $2^{s(q)}$, and this bound is attained for a positive proportion of eigenvalues. The conjecture proposes an upper bound complementary to the paper's lower bounds, attributing multiplicity to quadratic twisting; the source gives no resolution.

D32.title: Gross–Zagier and Gross–Kohnen–Zagier conjecture for CM values of weight-4 automorphic Green's functions
D32.statement:
Let $N\in\\{1,2,3,4\\}$, and let $z,z'\in\mathfrak H$ be quadratic irrational points satisfying

$$
[\mathbb Q(z):\mathbb Q]=[\mathbb Q(z'):\mathbb Q]=2.
$$

Assume that $z\notin\varGamma_0(N)z'$, where $\varGamma_0(N)$ is the Hecke congruence group of level $N$, and let $G^{\mathfrak H/\overline{\varGamma}_0(N)}_{2}(z,z')$ denote the weight-4 automorphic Green's function. **Gross–Zagier and Gross–Kohnen–Zagier conjecture.** The CM values are always expressible as logarithms of algebraic numbers, namely

$$
\exp\left[\operatorname{Im} z\operatorname{Im} z'G^{\mathfrak H/\overline{\varGamma}_0(N)}_{2}(z,z')\right]\in\overline{\mathbb Q}.
$$

This conjecture predicts an algebraicity phenomenon for automorphic Green's functions evaluated at pairs of CM points at the four levels for which the weight-4 cusp-form-free condition holds. The source presents it as an outstanding problem; no resolution is supplied here.

D32.title: Iwasawa-theoretic Mazur–Rubin–Sano congruence conjecture
D32.statement:
Let $L_n/L/k$, $V\subseteq V'$, $r$, $r'$, $e$, $\Gamma_n$, $\nu_n$, and $\mathcal{N}_n$ be as in the finite-level Mazur–Rubin–Sano setup, and let $\operatorname{Rec}_\infty$ be the inverse-limit reciprocity map. Assume the $p$-component Rubin–Stark conjecture for $L_n/k$ and $V$ for every $n$.

**Iwasawa-theoretic Mazur–Rubin–Sano conjecture.** There exists a unique

$$
\kappa=(\kappa_n)_n\in\bigcap^rU_{L,S,T}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_p}\varprojlim_n I(\Gamma_n)^e/I(\Gamma_n)^{e+1}
$$

such that $\nu_n(\kappa_n)=\mathcal{N}_n(\epsilon_{L_n/k,S,T}^V)$ for all $n$ and

$$
e_\chi\kappa=(-1)^{re}e_\chi\operatorname{Rec}_\infty(\epsilon_{L/k,S,T}^{V'}).
$$

This is the inverse-limit form of the finite-level congruence conjecture, encoding compatibility of Rubin–Stark elements across the Iwasawa tower.

D32.title: Kumar Murty's conjecture on rational Hecke eigenvalues
D32.statement:
Let $f$ be a weight $2$ normalized cuspidal Hecke eigenform of level $\Gamma_1(N)$ with quadratic coefficient field and without inner twists. Write $a_p(f)$ for its $p$-th Hecke coefficient. **Kumar Murty's conjecture.** There is a constant $c_f$ depending on $f$ such that

$$
\#\{p<x\text{ prime}\mid a_p(f)\in\mathds{Q}\}\sim c_f\frac{\sqrt{x}}{\log x}.
$$

This refines the known density-zero result for primes with rational coefficient and is part of a conjecture posed by Kumar Murty, building on work of S. Lang and H. Trotter. The source does not state a resolution.

D32.title: Topological invariance and existence conjecture for level-k series
D32.statement: Let $K$ be a knot, let $\zeta$ be a root of unity, and let $\gamma$ be a non-degenerate Neumann–Zagier datum arising from a triangulation of the knot complement. **Topological invariance conjecture.** For every knot $K$, there exists a triangulation with a non-degenerate Neumann–Zagier datum $\gamma$. The series $\phi_{\gamma,\zeta}(\hbar)$ is independent of the choice of triangulation and $\gamma$, up to multiplication by $\zeta^{1/12}$ and $e^{\hbar/(24k)}$; modulo these ambiguities it equals $\phi_{K,\zeta}(\hbar)$, the series on the right-hand side of the Quantum Modularity Conjecture. Experimental checks for many knots and state-integral invariance motivate the claim, but the assertion is not proved in general.

D32.title: Eichler–Shimura–Manin correspondence for newforms of levels 2 and 3
D32.statement:
Let $k$ be an even integer. For $N=2,3$, let $\mathcal S_k^{\mathrm{new}}(\Gamma_0(N))^{\pm}$ denote the subspaces of newforms on which the Atkin–Lehner involution acts by $\pm1$. Let $W_{2,\mathrm{new},\pm}^{\mathrm{ev},0}$ and $W_{3,\mathrm{new},\pm}^{\mathrm{ev},0}$ be the polynomial spaces defined by

$$
W_{2,\mathrm{new},\pm}^{\mathrm{ev},0}=\left\{p(x,y)\in\mathbb C[x,y]\ \middle|\ \begin{array}{l}-p(y,x)-p(y,x+y)+p(x,x+y)=-p(x,y),\\-p(y,2x)=\pm 2^{\frac{k-2}{2}}p(x,y)\end{array}\right\},
$$

and

$$
W_{3,\mathrm{new},\pm}^{\mathrm{ev},0}=\left\{p(x,y)\in\mathbb C[x,y]\ \middle|\ \begin{array}{l}-p(y,x)-p(y,x+y)+p(x,x+y)-p(y,x-y)+p(x,x-y)=-p(x,y),\\-p(y,3x)=\pm 3^{\frac{k-2}{2}}p(x,y)\end{array}\right\}.
$$

**Eichler–Shimura–Manin correspondence.** There are isomorphisms defined over $\mathbb C$

$$
\mathcal S_k^{\mathrm{new}}(\Gamma_0(2))^{\pm}\cong W_{2,\mathrm{new},\pm}^{\mathrm{ev},0},\qquad \mathcal S_k^{\mathrm{new}}(\Gamma_0(3))^{\pm}\cong W_{3,\mathrm{new},\pm}^{\mathrm{ev},0}.
$$

These conjectures arise from equations observed for restricted even period polynomials of newforms at levels $2$ and $3$, extending the correspondence between modular forms and period-polynomial spaces. The source reports them as natural conjectures but gives no resolution.

D32.title: Generating-series conjecture for newform dimensions at levels 2 and 3
D32.statement:
For $N=2,3$, let $\mathcal S_k^{\mathrm{new}}(\Gamma_0(N))^{\pm}$ denote the subspaces of newforms of weight $k$ and level $\Gamma_0(N)$ on which the Atkin–Lehner involution acts by $\pm1$. **Generating-series conjecture.** The generating series of their dimensions, for $k\geq6$, are

$$
\sum_{k=6}^{\infty}\dim\bigl(\mathcal S_k^{\mathrm{new}}(\Gamma_0(2))\bigr)^+x^k=\frac{x^8}{(1-x^6)(1-x^8)},
$$

$$
\sum_{k=6}^{\infty}\dim\bigl(\mathcal S_k^{\mathrm{new}}(\Gamma_0(2))\bigr)^-x^k=\frac{x^2(1+x^{18})}{(1-x^8)(1-x^{12})},
$$

$$
\sum_{k=6}^{\infty}\dim\bigl(\mathcal S_k^{\mathrm{new}}(\Gamma_0(3))\bigr)^+x^k=\frac{x^8}{(1-x^2)(1-x^{12})},
$$

$$
\sum_{k=6}^{\infty}\dim\bigl(\mathcal S_k^{\mathrm{new}}(\Gamma_0(3))\bigr)^-x^k=\frac{x^6(1+x^8+x^{10}-x^{12})}{(1-x^4)(1-x^{12})}.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by numerical agreement between eigenspace dimensions of the relevant matrices and dimensions of the corresponding newform spaces; the lower limit $k=6$ reflects the vanishing of the lower-weight newform spaces and the range in which the method applies. No resolution is supplied in the source.

D32.title: Replica-symmetry MP-structure conjecture for the independent set problem
D32.statement:
Let $(\beta,h,\gamma)$ be parameters of the independent set problem, and let an MP-structure consist of a hierarchy $(\zeta,\mathcal V_{\boldsymbol m})$ with $K$ levels. For such a structure, write $R_{N,\beta,h,\gamma}(\mathcal S)$ for the rest-term in the interpolation formula, where $\mathcal S=(\zeta,\mathcal V_{\boldsymbol m})$. **Replica-symmetry MP-structure conjecture.** For every $(\beta,h,\gamma)$ there exists a unique $K^\star$-level MP-structure $\mathcal S^\star=\mathcal S^\star(\beta,h,\gamma)=(\zeta^\star,\mathcal V^\star_{\boldsymbol m})$ such that

$$
\lim_{N\to\infty}R_{N,\beta,h,\gamma}(\mathcal S^\star)=0.
$$

The case $K^\star=\infty$ is also possible. This conjecture asserts that the limiting free energy is captured by a unique hierarchical MP-structure through the vanishing of the interpolation remainder, which is the key step in describing the replica-symmetry phase of the independent set problem.

D32.title: The quasi-irreducibility criterion for holomorphic eta quotients
D32.statement: Let $f$ be a holomorphic eta quotient of level $N$. It is **quasi-irreducible** if it is not factorizable on $\Gamma_0(N)$, whereas it is irreducible if its only factors are $1$ and $f$. **Quasi-irreducibility conjecture.** Every quasi-irreducible holomorphic eta quotient is irreducible. This is the contrapositive of the reducibility conjecture and would provide a direct algorithmic test for irreducibility at the given level; the source gives no resolution.

D32.title: Taylor's abelian-variety conjecture for modular eigenclasses over number fields
D32.statement:
Let $F$ be a number field, let ${\mathfrak p}$ be a prime of $F$, and let $\mathfrak m$ and $\mathfrak d$ be ideals as in the setup. Let $f\in H^{n+s}(\Gamma_0({\mathfrak p}\mathfrak m),{\mathbb C})$ be a nontrivial new eigenclass of level $\mathfrak N={\mathfrak p}\mathfrak m\mathfrak d$. Write $K_f={\mathbb Q}(\{a_{\mathfrak l}(f)\}_{{\mathfrak l}\nmid\mathfrak d})$ and $d=[K_f:{\mathbb Q}]$. **Taylor's conjecture.** One of the following holds: (1) there exists a simple abelian variety $A_f/F$ of dimension $d$ and conductor $\mathfrak N^d$ such that ${\mathbb Q}\otimes\operatorname{End}(A_f)$ contains $K_f$ and

$$
\# A_f({\mathcal O}_F/{\mathfrak l})=N_{K_f/{\mathbb Q}}(1+|{\mathfrak l}|-a_{\mathfrak l}(f))
$$

for all ${\mathfrak l}\nmid\mathfrak N$; or (2) there exists a simple abelian variety $A_f/F$ of dimension $2d$ and conductor $\mathfrak N^{2d}$, and a quaternion division algebra $D$ over $K_f$ such that ${\mathbb Q}\otimes\operatorname{End}(A_f)$ contains $D$ and

$$
\# A_f({\mathcal O}_F/{\mathfrak l})=N_{K_f/{\mathbb Q}}(1+|{\mathfrak l}|-a_{\mathfrak l}(f))^2
$$

for all ${\mathfrak l}\nmid\mathfrak N$. Moreover, $A_f$ does not have complex multiplication defined over $F$, and if $F$ has at least one real embedding then case (2) does not occur. This conjecturally attaches an abelian variety to a nontrivial new eigenclass, with the Hecke eigenvalues determining its local point counts and endomorphism algebra.

D32.title: All-level torsion growth conjecture for arithmetic groups
D32.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be an arithmetic group, let $\Gamma_k$ range over congruence subgroups of $\Gamma$ of increasing level, and let $\delta$ denote the deficiency of the associated real semisimple group. Let $i$ be the degree at the top of the cuspidal range, and let $\mathscr{L}$ be the coefficient lattice. **All-level torsion growth conjecture.** When $\delta=1$, the limit

$$
\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\frac{\log\lvert H^i(\Gamma_k;\mathscr{L})_{\operatorname{tors}}\rvert}{[\Gamma:\Gamma_k]}
$$

should equal the Bergeron–Venkatesh limit for any set of congruence subgroups of increasing level. In particular,

$$
\liminf_{\Gamma_k}\frac{\log\lvert H^i(\Gamma_k;\mathscr{L})_{\operatorname{tors}}\rvert}{[\Gamma:\Gamma_k]}
$$

taken over all congruence subgroups should equal that limit. This strengthens the prime-level version by allowing arbitrary increasing levels; the paper offers computational evidence, while the assertion remains unproved.

D32.title: The Taylor–Wiles-level Galois lifting conjecture
D32.statement:
Let $\overline{\rho}_{\mathfrak{m}}$ be the residual representation from the preceding conjecture, and let $(Q,(\gamma_{v,1},\dots,\gamma_{v,n})_{v\in Q})$ be a Taylor–Wiles datum. Let $G_{F,S\cup Q}$ be the Galois group unramified outside $S\cup Q$, and let ${\mathbb T}^{S\cup Q}(U^p_1(Q))_{\mathfrak{m}_{Q,1}}$ be the localized Taylor–Wiles-level Hecke algebra.

**Taylor–Wiles-level lifting conjecture.** If $\overline{\rho}_{\mathfrak{m}}$ is absolutely irreducible, there exists a continuous lifting

$$
\rho_{\mathfrak{m},Q}:G_{F,S\cup Q}\longrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_n({\mathbb T}^{S\cup Q}(U^p_1(Q))_{\mathfrak{m}_{Q,1}})
$$

whose Frobenius characteristic polynomial at every finite place $v\notin S\cup Q$ is

$$
X^n-T_v^1X^{n-1}+\cdots+(-1)^iq_v^{i(i-1)/2}T_v^iX^{n-i}+\cdots+(-1)^nq_v^{n(n-1)/2}T_v^n,
$$

and which is of type ${\mathcal S}_Q$.

This is the refinement of the global Galois representation conjecture required at Taylor–Wiles level. The paper assumes it and does not provide a resolution.

D32.title: The local-global compatibility conjecture at Taylor–Wiles level
D32.statement:
Let $(Q,(\gamma_{v,1},\dots,\gamma_{v,n})_{v\in Q})$ be a Taylor–Wiles datum, let $\sigma$ be an irreducible $E$-representation of $K_0$, and let $\sigma^\circ$ denote the associated integral lattice. Let $R_p^{\operatorname{loc}}(\sigma)$ be the corresponding quotient of $R_p^{\operatorname{loc}}$, let $\mathcal H(\sigma^\circ)$ be the Hecke algebra, and let $\eta$ be the indicated map from this Hecke algebra to the local deformation ring.

**Local-global compatibility conjecture.** The action of $R_p^{\operatorname{loc}}$ on

$$
H_*(X_{K_0U^p_1(Q)},\sigma^\circ)_{\mathfrak m_{Q,1}}
$$

factors through $R_p^{\operatorname{loc}}(\sigma)$. Moreover, if $h\in\mathcal H(\sigma^\circ)$ satisfies $\eta(h)\in R_p^{\operatorname{loc}}(\sigma)$, then $h$ acts on

$$
H_{q_0}(X_{K_0U^p_1(Q)},\sigma^\circ)_{\mathfrak m_{Q,1}}
$$

via $\eta(h)$.

This is formulated as a refinement of the earlier Galois and Taylor–Wiles compatibility conjectures. It is intended to provide the local-global compatibility needed to deduce the general $p$-adic local Langlands action; the supplied text gives no resolution.

D32.title: Random permutation model for Hecke operators modulo prime level
D32.statement: Let $p$ be a prime and write $D_p^\pm=\dim_{\mathbb{Q}}S_2(\Gamma_0(p);\mathbb{Q})^\pm$. Fix a prime $\ell$. Let $\sigma_+$ and $\sigma_-$ be independently chosen uniformly random permutations on $D_p^+$ and $D_p^-$ elements. **Random permutation model conjecture.** The factorization type of the characteristic polynomial of $T_\ell$ acting on $S_2(\Gamma_0(p);\mathbb{F}_p)$ is distributed like the cycle type of $\sigma_+\sqcup\sigma_-$. This heuristic models the reduced Hecke algebras on the two Atkin–Lehner eigenspaces as independent random étale algebras and is used to predict the distribution of large irreducible factors.

D32.title: The $p=2$ ghost conjecture for modular-form slopes
D32.statement:
Let $N$ be a positive integer and let $\kappa\in\mathcal{W}$. Let $G_\kappa^{\circ}$ be the specialization of the modified ghost series for $p=2$, let $P_\kappa$ be the characteristic power series of the $U_2$-operator, and write $\operatorname{NP}$ for the Newton polygon. The prime $2$ is **$\Gamma_0(N)$-regular** when the corresponding regularity condition holds.

**The $p=2$ ghost conjecture.** If $2$ is $\Gamma_0(N)$-regular, then

$$
\operatorname{NP}(G_\kappa^{\circ})=\operatorname{NP}(P_\kappa)
$$

for every $\kappa\in\mathcal{W}$.

The modified series incorporates extra multiplicities at the relevant weight-space points and is designed to match the observed boundary slopes for level $\Gamma_1(8N)$. The assertion extends the ghost-series prediction to the $p=2$ setting.

D32.title: Thomas's local negative-circuit conjecture for sustained oscillations
D32.statement: Let $f$ be a Boolean evolution function with asynchronous state transition graph $\Gamma(f)$ and local, or type-1, functional circuits in its interaction graph. A type-1 functional circuit is a circuit whose arcs are all functional at the same state of the system's state transition graph. **Thomas's local negative-circuit conjecture.** If $\Gamma(f)$ has a cyclic attractor, then the interaction graph has a type-1 functional negative circuit. The conjecture concerns the connection between sustained oscillations and regulatory circuits. The corresponding global statement is known, and a multilevel counter-example to the local statement was known; the existence of Boolean counter-examples was left open in the cited work and is addressed by the paper's counter-example.

D32.title: The congruence-kernel conjecture for super-modular categories
D32.statement:
Let $\mathcal{B}$ be a super-modular category of rank $2k$, and let $\hat{S}$ and $\hat{T}^2$ be the corresponding matrices. Let $\Gamma_\theta=\langle\mathfrak{s},\mathfrak{t}^2\rangle<\operatorname{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ be the spin mapping class group of the torus with spin structure $(A,A)$, and let $\pi_k$ denote passage to $\operatorname{PSU}(k)$. **The congruence-kernel conjecture.** The projective representation

$$
\hat{\rho}:\Gamma_\theta\longrightarrow \operatorname{PSU}(k),\qquad \hat{\rho}(\mathfrak{s})=\pi_k(\hat{S}),\quad \hat{\rho}(\mathfrak{t}^2)=\pi_k(\hat{T}^2)
$$

has kernel a congruence subgroup. If true, the image $\hat{\rho}(\Gamma_\theta)$ is finite; the level of the kernel is not known in general.

D32.title: Modularity conjecture for rigid Calabi–Yau threefolds
D32.statement:
Recall that a smooth, projective threefold $X$ is a **Calabi–Yau threefold** if its canonical bundle is trivial and $H^{1}(X,\mathcal{O}_{X})=H^{2}(X,\mathcal{O}_{X})=0$. It is **rigid** if $H^{1}(X,\mathcal{T}_{X})=0$. For a rigid Calabi–Yau threefold defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, let $L(X,s)$ denote its $L$-series.

**Modularity conjecture.** Any rigid Calabi–Yau threefold $X$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$ is modular: its $L$-series $L(X,s)$ coincides up to finitely many Euler factors with the Mellin transform $L(f,s)$ of a modular cusp form $f$ of weight $4$ with respect to $\Gamma_{0}(N)$, where the level $N$ is only divisible by the primes of bad reduction.

This conjecture predicts that arithmetic data from rigid Calabi–Yau threefolds over $\mathbb{Q}$ are governed by weight-$4$ modular forms. The paper constructs examples realizing some new weight-$4$ cusp forms, while the general modularity assertion remains open.

D32.title: Yoshida-lift generation conjecture for vector-valued Siegel modular forms
D32.statement: Let $S_{j,2}(Gamma_2[2])$ denote the space of vector-valued Siegel modular forms of degree $2$, weight $(j,2)$, and level $Gamma_2[2]$. A **Yoshida-lift generation conjecture.** The space $S_{j,2}(Gamma_2[2])$ is generated by Yoshida type lifts. The preceding theorem describes the relevant Yoshida lifts and their multiplicities in the cases where they occur; the conjecture asserts that these lifts account for the whole space.

D32.title: Ribet-style level-lowering conjecture for Bianchi newforms
D32.statement:
Let $F$ be a weight $2$ Bianchi newform of level $\Gamma_0(\operatorname{id}{n}\operatorname{id}{p})$, where $\operatorname{id}{p}$ is a prime number, and let $\ell\geq 5$ be a prime. Suppose that the residual representation of $\rho_{F,\ell}$ is absolutely irreducible and finite at $\operatorname{id}{p}$. Then there is an automorphic form

$$
G\in H^1(Y_0(\operatorname{id}{n}),\mathbb F_{\ell})
$$

whose Galois representation is isomorphic to $\overline{\rho_{F,\ell}}$.

**Ribet-style level-lowering conjecture.** Under these hypotheses, such an automorphic form $G$ exists at level with the prime factor $\operatorname{id}{p}$ removed.

This conjecture is presented as an analogue of Ribet's classical level-lowering result for Bianchi modular forms; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

D32.title: Bloch–Kato conjecture for Hilbert modular forms
D32.statement:
Let $g$ be a normalised cuspidal Hilbert modular newform of weight $(k_1,k_2,\ldots,k_d,w=2)$ and level $\Gamma_0(\mathfrak{n})$ over a totally real number field $F$, with each $k_i$ even and with associated automorphic representation having trivial central character. Let $E$ be the totally real number field generated by the Hecke eigenvalues $t_v(g)$. For a finite place $\lambda$ of $E$ with residue characteristic $p$, let $V_{g,\lambda}$ be the associated two-dimensional $E_\lambda$-representation, and let $H^1_f(F,V_{g,\lambda})$ denote its Bloch–Kato Selmer group. The $L$-functions are normalised so that, at good places, 
$$
L_v(V_{g,\lambda},s)=L_v(g,s)=\left(1-t_vq_v^{-s-1}+q_v^{-2s-1}\right)^{-1}.
$$
 **Bloch–Kato conjecture.** 
$$
\dim_{E_\lambda}H^1_f(F,V_{g,\lambda})=\operatorname{ord}_{s=0}L(V_{g,\lambda},s),
$$
 equivalently, 
$$
\dim_{E_\lambda}H^1_f(F,V_{g,\lambda})=\operatorname{ord}_{s=0}L(g,s).
$$
 This predicts that the dimension of the Bloch–Kato Selmer group equals the central order of vanishing of the relevant $L$-function. The statement is presented as a conjecture in the source; no resolution evidence is supplied here.

D32.title: Conjecture on Tracy–Widom fluctuations in the i.i.d. model
D32.statement: Let $G_n$ be the hexagonal-lattice rhombus with $2n-1$ levels, and let $H_n$ be its weighted adjacency operator. In the i.i.d. model, all edge weights are independent copies of a nonzero almost surely real-valued random variable $X$ satisfying the stated exponential moment conditions. Let $\bar f$ and $\bar g$ denote appropriate constants for the distribution of $X$. **The i.i.d. model conjecture.** Theorem's Tracy–Widom limit for the mixed model also holds in the i.i.d. model, with $\bar f$ and $\bar g$ replaced by appropriate constants; equivalently, the centered and scaled smallest positive eigenvalue has the corresponding GUE Tracy–Widom limiting distribution. The mixed-model theorem establishes this fluctuation behavior for Gamma-distributed blue-edge weights and unit red-edge weights, whereas the analogous result for general i.i.d. edge weights remains conjectural.

D32.title: Degree and linear-factor conjecture for class 3C supersingular polynomials
D32.statement:
Let $p\geq5$ be prime. Let $ss_{p}^{(3C)}(X)$ be the supersingular polynomial associated with the group $\Gamma_{0}(3|3)$, and let $L^{(3C)}(p)$ be its number of linear factors. Let $L(p)$ denote the number of linear factors of the level-1 supersingular polynomial.

**Class 3C supersingular-polynomial conjecture.**

$$
\deg ss_{p}^{(3C)}(X)=\frac{p-1}{4}+\frac32\varepsilon,\qquad L^{(3C)}(p)=\left(2+\left(\frac{-3}{p}\right)\right)L(p).
$$

This conjecture predicts both the degree and the number of linear factors for the class-3C supersingular polynomial. The source gives no resolution evidence, and the supplied context does not define $\varepsilon$.

D32.title: Tsaknias's generalized Maeda conjecture for square-free levels
D32.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$ be even and sufficiently large, and let $N$ be square-free. Write $d_{k,N}$ for the dimension of the largest simple Hecke submodule of $S_k(\Gamma_0(N))$, and let $\omega(N)$ denote the number of distinct prime divisors of $N$. **Tsaknias's generalized Maeda conjecture.** The number of Galois orbits of newforms in $S_k(\Gamma_0(N))$ is $2^{\omega(N)}$. In particular, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, there is a constant $c(k,\varepsilon)>0$, depending at most on $k$ and $\varepsilon$, such that

$$
d_{k,N}>c(k,\varepsilon)N^{1-\varepsilon}
$$

for all square-free $N\geq 1$. This generalizes Maeda's conjecture to square-free levels, where Atkin--Lehner involutions provide the expected obstruction to simplicity; the parser supplies no evidence resolving the claim.

D32.title: Conjectures on Hecke operators, diagonalizability, and oldforms for Drinfeld cusp forms
D32.statement:
Let $q$ be the cardinality of the coefficient field, let $t$ be the level-one prime, and let $S^1_{k,m}(GL_2(A))$ and $S^1_{k,m}(\Gamma_0(t))$ denote the corresponding spaces of Drinfeld cusp forms of weight $k$ and type $m$. Write $\mathbf{T}_t$ for the Hecke operator at $t$, $\mathbf{U}_t$ for the level-$t$ operator, and $S^{1,old}_{k,m}(\Gamma_0(t))$ and $S^{1,new}_{k,m}(\Gamma_0(t))$ for the oldform and newform subspaces, with $\delta$ the degeneracy-map construction and $Tr,Tr'$ the trace and twisted-trace maps.

**The oldform and Hecke conjectures.** The following assertions should hold:

$$
\operatorname{Ker}(\mathbf{T}_t)=0;
$$

$\mathbf{U}_t$ is diagonalizable when $q$ is odd and, when $q$ is even, it is diagonalizable if and only if the dimension of $S^{1,new}_{k,m}(\Gamma_0(t))$ is $1$; and

$$
S^1_{k,m}(\Gamma_0(t))=S^{1,old}_{k,m}(\Gamma_0(t))\oplus S^{1,new}_{k,m}(\Gamma_0(t))=\operatorname{Im}(\delta)\oplus(\operatorname{Ker}(Tr)\cap\operatorname{Ker}(Tr')).
$$

These conjectures are motivated by numerical data and comparison with the classical case. Non-diagonalizability is known in even characteristic and appears related to the antidiagonal action of $\mathbf{U}_t$ on newforms; the proposed decomposition and injectivity remain unresolved in the source.

D32.title: The TMF splitting conjecture for modular curves of level \a0n
D32.statement:
For $n\geq 1$, let $\operatorname{TMF}_0(n)_{(3)}$ and $\operatorname{Tmf}_0(n)_{(3)}$ denote the level-$\Gamma_0(n)$ topological modular forms spectra localized at $3$, and let $\operatorname{TMF}_1(2)_{(3)}$ and $\operatorname{Tmf}_1(2)_{(3)}$ denote the corresponding level-$\Gamma_1(2)$ spectra. Let $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_0(n)$ be the compactified moduli stack of elliptic curves with $\Gamma_0(n)$-structure, and let $\underline{\omega}$ be the Hodge line bundle.

**TMF splitting conjecture.** The $\operatorname{TMF}_{(3)}$-module $\operatorname{TMF}_0(n)_{(3)}$ decomposes into possibly shifted copies of $\operatorname{TMF}_1(2)_{(3)}$ and of $\operatorname{TMF}_{(3)}$. If $H^1(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_0(n);\underline{\omega})$ has no $3$-torsion, the $\operatorname{Tmf}_{(3)}$-module $\operatorname{Tmf}_0(n)_{(3)}$ decomposes into possibly shifted copies of $\operatorname{Tmf}_1(2)_{(3)}$ and into invertible $\operatorname{Tmf}_{(3)}$-modules.

This conjecture generalizes the proved splitting for $n=7$ and would extend known prime-local splitting results for topological modular forms. The stated condition on $H^1$ ensures that the connective splitting can include invertible $\operatorname{Tmf}_{(3)}$-modules; the conjecture is presented as open in the source.

D32.title: Benjamini–Yadin cylinder growth conjecture for external DLA
D32.statement:
Let $(\mathcal{G}^n)_{n\geq 0}$ be a family of $d$-regular graphs with $|\mathcal{G}^n|\to\infty$. For each $n$, form the cylinder graph $\mathcal{G}^n\times\mathbb{N}$, let $(\mathcal{E}_t)$ be external DLA started from the zero layer, and let $T_m$ be the first time the cluster reaches level $m$. **Benjamini–Yadin's cylinder growth conjecture.** There exist $0<\gamma<1$ and $n_0$ such that, for every $n>n_0$ and every $m$, 

$$
\mathbb{E}[T_m]\leq m|\mathcal{G}^n|^\gamma.
$$

The theorem preceding the conjecture gives a weaker bound for rapidly mixing regular bases; the conjecture seeks sublinear-than-the-base-size growth per level in general for such graph families.

D32.title: Ratios-model formula for the averaged one-level density of Hecke L-functions
D32.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}(K)=\{L_k(s):1\le k\le K\}$, let $M=\log K$, and let $R_K(\alpha,\gamma)$ be the ratios-conjecture prediction built from the Euler product $G(\alpha,\gamma)$. For shifts satisfying the constraints in the ratios domain, **the ratios-model one-level-density conjecture.**

$$
R_K(\alpha,\gamma)=G(\alpha,\gamma)+\frac{1}{1-2\alpha}\left(\frac{\pi}{2K}\right)^{2\alpha}G(-\alpha,\gamma)+O(K^{-\frac12+\epsilon}).
$$

Here

$$
G(\alpha,\gamma)=\left(1-\frac{1}{2^{1+\gamma+\alpha}}\right)\prod_{p\equiv1(4)}\left(1-\frac{2}{p^{1+\gamma+\alpha}}+\frac{1}{p^{1+2\gamma}}\right)\prod_{p\equiv3(4)}\left(1-\frac{1}{p^{1+2\gamma}}\right)\prod_p\left(1-\frac{1}{p^{1+2\alpha}}\right)^{-1}.
$$

This is an intermediate ratios-conjecture prediction used to obtain lower-order terms in the one-level density; the source gives no independent resolution status.

D32.title: Conjectural one-level density formula for the family $\mathcal{F}(K)$
D32.statement:
Let $\mathcal{F}(K)=\{L_k(s):1\le k\le K\}$, let $M=\log K$, let $f$ be the test function, and let $W_f$, $S_\zeta$, $S_L$, $S_{A'}$, and $S_\Gamma$ be the integrals defined in the source, with $(\mathcal{C}')$ the horizontal line $\operatorname{Im}(\tau)=-Mc'/\pi$. **Conjectural one-level density formula.**

$$
D_1(\mathcal{F}(K);f)=W_f+S_\zeta+S_L+S_{A'}+S_\Gamma+O\left(K^{-\frac12+\epsilon}\right).
$$

The formula assembles the gamma-factor, zeta-factor, auxiliary $L$-function, and arithmetic contributions predicted by the ratios calculation; the source gives no resolution status.

D32.title: Squarefree-level weight-four Eisenstein congruence conjecture
D32.statement:
Let $N_1$ and $N_2$ be coprime squarefree positive integers, with $\omega(N_1)$ odd, and let $E_4$ be the weight-$4$ Eisenstein series on $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$. **Squarefree-level weight-four congruence conjecture.** If $p$ is an odd prime dividing

$$
\frac{1}{45}\prod_{\ell\mid N_1}(\ell^2-1)\prod_{\ell\mid N_2}(\ell^2+1),
$$

then there exists an eigenform $f\in S_4(\Gamma_0(N_1N_2))$ Hecke congruent to $E_4$ modulo $p$. If $p\ge7$ and $p\mid(\ell^2-1)$ for every $\ell\mid N_1$ while $p\mid(\ell^2+1)$ for every $\ell\mid N_2$, $f$ may be chosen new of level $N_1N_2$, with Atkin--Lehner sign $-1$ at primes dividing $N_1$ and $+1$ at primes dividing $N_2$. This is presented as a weight-four generalization of the cited prime-level Eisenstein congruence theorem and is intended to explain congruences arising from the SO(5) mass formula; its general validity is not established in the supplied text.

D32.title: Lee–Szczarba conjecture on top-dimensional cohomology of congruence subgroups
D32.statement:
Let $\Gamma_n(p)$ be the level-$p$ principal congruence subgroup of $\operatorname{SL}_n(\mathbb{Z})$, and let ${\mathcal{T}}_n(\mathbb{Q})$ be the Tits building of $\operatorname{SL}_n(\mathbb{Q})$. Write

$$
\operatorname{St}_n(\mathbb{Q})=\widetilde{\operatorname{H}}_{n-2}({\mathcal{T}}_n(\mathbb{Q})).
$$

The quotient map from ${\mathcal{T}}_n(\mathbb{Q})$ to ${\mathcal{T}}_n(\mathbb{Q})/\Gamma_n(p)$ induces a map on reduced homology.

**Lee–Szczarba conjecture.** For a prime $p$ and $n\geq 2$, the induced map

$$
(\operatorname{St}_n(\mathbb{Q}))_{\Gamma_n(p)}\longrightarrow \widetilde{\operatorname{H}}_{n-2}({\mathcal{T}}_n(\mathbb{Q})/\Gamma_n(p))
$$

is an isomorphism. Equivalently, the top-dimensional cohomology group $\operatorname{H}^{\binom{n}{2}}(\Gamma_n(p))$ is isomorphic to $\widetilde{\operatorname{H}}_{n-2}({\mathcal{T}}_n(\mathbb{Q})/\Gamma_n(p))$.

The conjecture identifies all top-dimensional cohomology with the coinvariants of the rational Steinberg module. The source states that it was proved for $p=3$, while the paper explains that larger primes require additional cohomology beyond the Steinberg module over $\mathbb{F}_p$; the supplied text does not establish a complete resolution for all primes.

D32.title: The asymptotic tightness conjecture for domination lower bounds
D32.statement:
Fix integers $k$ and $\ell$ with

$$
k>\ell\ge 2.
$$

Let $G_{k,\ell}$ be the two-level cube graph considered in the paper, let $\gamma(G_{k,\ell})$ denote its domination number, and let the lower bound referred to in Theorem~ be the paper's stated lower bound. **The asymptotic tightness conjecture.** The lower bound given in Theorem~ is asymptotically tight for all fixed $k>\ell\ge 2$ as $n\to\infty$.
This is a broad conjecture that the paper's general lower bound captures the correct asymptotic domination number for every fixed pair; no resolution is supplied in the excerpt.

D32.title: Gouvêa's limiting-measure conjecture for supersingularities
D32.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime number, and let $\k\geqslant 2$ and $N$ be positive integers with $N$ coprime to $p$. For weight $k$ and level $\Gamma_0(Np)$ eigenforms, define the supersingularity of an eigenform of slope $v$ to be $\frac{v}{k-1}$, and let $\mu_k$ be the discrete probability measure on $[0,1]$ obtained by placing a point mass at each supersingularity. For $N=1$, the conjecture concerns the sequence $(\mu_l)_{l\geqslant 2}$. **Gouvêa's conjecture.** The sequence $(\mu_l)_{l\geqslant 2}$ converges to the uniform measure on

$$
[0,\frac{1}{p+1}]\cup[\frac{p}{p+1},1].
$$

This predicts the limiting distribution suggested by computations of supersingularities of eigenforms, including the concentration near the two indicated intervals as the weight tends to infinity. The parser provides no evidence resolving the conjecture.

D32.title: Heuristic for counting elliptic curves with prescribed level structures
D32.statement:
Let $\mathcal{Z}_{1,\mathbb{Q}}^{[\Gamma]}(\mathcal{B})$ count generalized elliptic curves with $[\Gamma]$-structures over $\mathbb{Z}$ ordered by $0<\operatorname{ht}(\Delta_1)\leq\mathcal{B}$. **Heuristic for elliptic curves with level structures.** The following asymptotic-tightness estimates are expected:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{Z}_{1,\mathbb{Q}}^{[\Gamma_1(2)]}(\mathcal{B})&\sim_{\mathcal{O}(1)}a\mathcal{B}^{\frac12}+b,\\
\mathcal{Z}_{1,\mathbb{Q}}^{[\Gamma_1(3)]}(\mathcal{B})&\sim_{\mathcal{O}(1)}a\mathcal{B}^{\frac13}+b,\\
\mathcal{Z}_{1,\mathbb{Q}}^{[\Gamma_1(4)]}(\mathcal{B})&\sim_{\mathcal{O}(1)}a\mathcal{B}^{\frac14}+b,\\
\mathcal{Z}_{1,\mathbb{Q}}^{[\Gamma(2)]}(\mathcal{B})&\sim_{\mathcal{O}(1)}a\mathcal{B}^{\frac13}+b.
\end{aligned}
$$

These estimates arise in the appendix from finite-field counting results and the global-fields analogy; the source gives no resolution.

D32.title: The total Roman domination join conjecture
D32.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $k$ be its total Roman domination parameter in the sense that $G$ is $k$-$\gamma_{tR}$-edge-supercritical. Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $G\cup K_n$ denote their disjoint union. A graph is **$k$-$\gamma_{tR}$-edge-supercritical** when its total Roman domination edge-supercriticality is measured at level $k$.

**Join conjecture.** If $G$ is a $k$-$\gamma_{tR}$-edge-supercritical graph, then $G\cup K_n$ is $(k+3)$-$\gamma_{tR}$-edge-critical, for $n\geq3$.

The conjecture generalizes the preceding constructions involving disjoint unions with complete graphs. The source states that it would follow directly from the first conjecture and gives no resolution.

D32.title: The Atkin–Lehner equidistribution conjecture for level-2 modular forms
D32.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$, and let $S_k(\Gamma_0(2))$ be the space of cusp forms of weight $k$ and level $2$. Let $W_2$ denote the Atkin–Lehner operator, and set

$$
d=\dim_\mathbb{C}S_k(\Gamma_0(2)).
$$

**Atkin–Lehner equidistribution conjecture.** For all $k\geq 2$, the space $S_k(\Gamma_0(2))$ decomposes under $W_2$ into Hecke-irreducible subspaces of dimensions $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$ and $\lceil d/2\rceil$.

This is an analogue of the Maeda conjecture for level $2$, predicting that the Hecke-irreducible pieces in the two Atkin–Lehner eigenspaces are as evenly sized as possible. The source reports computational evidence through weight $400$, while the assertion is not established in general.

D32.title: The Steinberg-homology conjecture for real quadratic fields
D32.statement:
Let $N$ be a level, let $E$ be a real quadratic field, and let $\psi_{\Gamma,E}$ denote the map associated with a subgroup $\Gamma$ as in the conjecture. Write $A_E(N)$ and $A_E(N)^*$ for the subgroups defined in the paper, and let $H_0^{\mathrm{cusp}}(\Gamma, \operatorname{St}(\mathbb{Q}^2;\mathbb{Z}))$ denote cuspidal degree-zero homology with coefficients in the Steinberg module. **Conjecture.** For any level $N$ and real quadratic field $E$: (1) if $\Gamma=\Gamma_1(N)^\pm$ or $\Gamma_1(N)$, then

$$
\psi_{\Gamma,E}:\text{(source)}\longrightarrow H_0^{\mathrm{cusp}}(\Gamma, \operatorname{St}(\mathbb{Q}^2;\mathbb{Z}))
$$

is surjective; (2) the cokernel of $\psi_{\Gamma_0(N)^\pm,E}$ is isomorphic to a quotient of

$$
\bigl((\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^\times/\{\pm1\}\bigr)/A_E(N);
$$

and (3) the cokernel of $\psi_{\Gamma_0(N),E}$ is isomorphic to a quotient of

$$
(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^\times/A_E(N)^*.
$$

The conjecture extends the preceding computational and conditional results without assuming GRH. The source does not define the source of $\psi_{\Gamma,E}$ or the groups $A_E(N)$ and $A_E(N)^*$ in the supplied excerpt, so these definitions and the status of the conjecture should be checked against the full paper.

D32.title: Scaling-limit conjecture for the unlabelled $(\alpha,\gamma)$-chain
D32.statement: Let $0 < \gamma \leq \alpha < 1$. Consider the unlabelled $(\alpha,\gamma)$-chain on rooted multifurcating trees with $n$ leaves, obtained by selecting and deleting a uniform leaf and inserting a new leaf according to the unlabelled $(\alpha,\gamma)$-growth rule. Represent its edges at scale $n^\gamma$, and view the resulting weighted trees in the Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov space of weighted $\mathbb{R}$-trees. **The unlabelled $(\alpha,\gamma)$-chain scaling-limit conjecture.** The unlabelled $(\alpha,\gamma)$-chain with $n^2$ steps per time unit and edges scaled by $n^\gamma$ has a scaling limit that is a path-continuous Markov process in the Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov space of weighted $\mathbb{R}$-trees, whose stationary distribution is that of $\mathcal{T}^{\alpha,\gamma}$. The conjecture extends the finite-dimensional Wright-Fisher diffusion limit for decorated projections and the stationary Gromov-Hausdorff-Prokhorov convergence to a dynamical continuum-tree limit; neither the asserted process-level convergence nor the required path continuity is established in the supplied text.

D32.title: Integrality and irreducibility conjecture for level-$N$ class polynomials
D32.statement:
Let $D$ and $N$ be as in the source, let $m\in\mathcal{M}_{D,N}$, and let $j_N^+$ be a Hauptmodul for $\Gamma_0^+(N)$. Define

$$
H_{D,N,m}(X)=\prod_{Q\in\mathcal{Q}_{D,N,m}^0/\Gamma_0^+(N)}\left(X-j_N^+(\tau_Q)\right).
$$

**Class-polynomial conjecture.** The polynomial $H_{D,N,m}(X)$ belongs to $\mathbb{Z}[X]$ and is irreducible. This is proposed as an analogue of the preceding classical class-polynomial theorem; the source gives no resolution of the assertion.

D32.title: Modularity conjecture for elliptic curves over function fields
D32.statement: Let $X$ be a smooth, projective, geometrically irreducible curve with function field $K$, and let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $K$ with conductor $N$ and irreducible associated Galois representation. Let $\overline{\operatorname{Sht}}^2(\Gamma_0(N))$ denote the compactified moduli space of shtukas with level $\Gamma_0(N)$. **Modularity conjecture.** There exists a special kind of correspondence between $E\times E$ and $\overline{\operatorname{Sht}}^2(\Gamma_0(N))$. This conjectural correspondence is presented as a motivation for studying rank-two shtuka moduli spaces; no construction or resolution is supplied in the text.

D32.title: Heuristic one-level density formula for logarithmic derivatives in cubic field families
D32.statement:
Let $\frac 12 \leq \theta<\frac 56$ and $\omega\geq0$ be such that the stated local estimate holds. Let $\mathcal F^\pm(X)$ be the family of cubic fields of discriminant of sign $\pm$ and size at most $X$, with cardinality $N^\pm(X)$. For the associated Artin representations $f_K$, let $\theta_e$, $x_p$, $\beta_e(p)$, $C_1^\pm$, $C_2^\pm$, $A_3$, $A_4$, $\Gamma_\pm$, and $L$ be the quantities defined in the paper. There exists $0<\delta<\frac 16$ such that, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and $r\in\mathbb C$ satisfying $\frac1L\ll\operatorname{Re}(r)<\delta$ and $|r|\leq X^{\varepsilon/2}$, an asymptotic formula for the family average of $L'(\frac12+r,f_K)/L(\frac12+r,f_K)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac1{N^\pm(X)}\sum_{K\in\mathcal F^\pm(X)}\frac{L'(\frac12+r,f_K)}{L(\frac12+r,f_K)}={}&-\sum_{p,e\geq1}\left(\theta_e+\frac1p\right)\frac{x_p\log p}{p^{e(\frac12+r)}}\\
&-\frac{C_2^\pm}{C_1^\pm}X^{-\frac16}\left(1-\frac{C_2^\pm}{C_1^\pm}X^{-\frac16}\right)\sum_{p,e\geq1}\frac{(\beta_e(p)-p^{-e/3})\log p}{p^{e(\frac12+r)}}\\
&+\frac{C_2^\pm}{C_1^\pm}X^{-\frac16}\left(1-\frac{C_2^\pm}{C_1^\pm}X^{-\frac16}\right)\frac{\zeta'}\zeta\left(\frac56+r\right)\\
&-X^{-r}\frac{\Gamma_\pm(\frac12-r)}{\Gamma_\pm(\frac12+r)}\zeta(1-2r)\frac{A_3(-r,r)}{1-r}\\
&-\frac{C_2^\pm}{C_1^\pm}X^{-r-\frac16}\left(1-\frac{C_2^\pm}{C_1^\pm}X^{-\frac16}\right)\frac{\Gamma_\pm(\frac12-r)}{\Gamma_\pm(\frac12+r)}\zeta(1-2r)\\
&\qquad\times\left(\frac{\zeta(\frac56-r)}{\zeta(\frac56+r)}\frac{A_4(-r,r)}{1-\frac{6r}{5}}-\frac{A_3(-r,r)}{1-r}\right)+O_\varepsilon(X^{\theta-1+\varepsilon}).
\end{aligned}
$$

**The one-level density conjecture.** The displayed asymptotic formula should hold, and the two sums on its right-hand side are absolutely convergent.

The formula is a conjectural refinement of the family average of logarithmic derivatives, incorporating the lower-order terms of size $X^{-1/6}$ and the secondary zeta-factor contribution. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

D32.title: The local-global conjecture for traces in the commutator subgroup of \(\Gamma(2)\)
D32.statement: Let $\Gamma(2)'$ be the commutator subgroup of the level-2 principal congruence subgroup $\Gamma(2)\subset\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, and let an integer $t$ be **admissible** if, for every $q\geq1$, it belongs to $\operatorname{Tr}(\Gamma(2)')\bmod q$. **The local-global trace conjecture.** For all sufficiently large admissible $t$, there exists $\gamma\in\Gamma(2)'$ such that $\operatorname{Tr}(\gamma)=t$. The admissibility theorem identifies the local congruence conditions, while the global assertion that every sufficiently large admissible trace occurs remains unresolved.

D32.title: Perron's conjecture on the mod-p extension of the Casson invariant
D32.statement:
Let $g\geq 3$ and let $p\geq 5$ be prime. Let $\mathcal{M}_{g,1}[p]$ be the mod-$p$ Torelli group, $\mathcal{T}_{g,1}$ the Torelli group, and $D_{g,1}[p]$ the subgroup generated by $p$-powers of Dehn twists. For $S^3_\varphi\in\mathcal{S}^3[p]$ with $\varphi=f\cdot m$, where $f\in\mathcal{T}_{g,1}$ and $m\in D_{g,1}[p]$, define $\gamma_p:\mathcal{M}_{g,1}[p]\to\mathbb{Z}/p$ by

$$
\gamma_p(\varphi)=\lambda(S^3_f)\pmod p.
$$

**Perron's conjecture.** The map $\gamma_p$ is a well-defined invariant on $\mathcal{S}^3[p]$. Perron proposed this as an extension of the Casson invariant to the mod-$p$ Torelli group. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

D32.title: The general Morava character-formula conjecture
D32.statement:
Let $w$ be a dominant weight, let $n$ be the relevant level, and let $L_w^{(n)}(\gamma,\mathbb{F})$ be the representation associated with a group homomorphism $\gamma$. Write $\operatorname{ch}(L_w^{(n)}(\gamma,\mathbb{F}))$ for its character and $E_w^{(n)}$ for Lusztig's character formula.

**General character-formula conjecture.** For general $w$, there exists a group homomorphism $\gamma$ such that

$$
\operatorname{ch}(L_w^{(n)}(\gamma,\mathbb{F}))=E_w^{(n)}.
$$

The paper says this follows immediately from the reduced-weight conjecture and the displayed character factorization formula. The supplied text does not state whether either conjecture has been resolved.

D32.title: The BS/PT wall-crossing formula with insertions
D32.statement:
Let $X$ be a projective threefold with Gorenstein and rational singularities, let $f:Y\to X$ be a resolution of singularities of relative dimension $1$, and let $Y$ be a projective Calabi–Yau threefold. For insertions $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_r\in f^*H^{\cdot}(X,\mathbb{Z})$ and descendant levels $\kappa_1,\ldots,\kappa_r\geqslant 0$, write $\mathrm{BS}^f(q;\gamma,\kappa)$ and $\mathrm{PT}^{Y}(q;\gamma,\kappa)$ for the corresponding generating series, and write $\mathrm{PT}^{Y,\mathrm{exc}}(q)$ for the exceptional PT generating series. **BS/PT wall-crossing formula with insertions.** The generating series satisfy

$$
\mathrm{BS}^f(q;\gamma,\kappa)=\frac{\mathrm{PT}^{Y}(q;\gamma,\kappa)}{\mathrm{PT}^{Y,\mathrm{exc}}(q)}.
$$

This extends the Bryan–Steinberg wall-crossing formula from invariants without insertions to arbitrary descendant insertions pulled back from $X$. The source presents the formula as a conjectural statement; its validity concerns the compatibility of the BS/PT wall crossing with descendants in the relative Calabi–Yau resolution setting.

D32.title: The sparse-presentation conjecture for the J-induced map on the Nakaoka module
D32.statement: Let the Nakaoka module be presented using generators including $\gamma_{1[1]}^{2^k-1}$, and consider the map induced by the $J$-homomorphism. **Sparse-presentation conjecture.** There exists a presentation of the Nakaoka module such that every generator other than $\gamma_{1[1]}^{2^k-1}$ maps to $0$ under the map induced by the $J$-homomorphism. The paper offers this as an apparent structural explanation for the behavior seen at the level of resolutions, but does not prove the existence of such a presentation.

D32.title: Bandini–Valentino's Atkin–Lehner conjecture for Drinfeld modular forms at level T
D32.statement:
Let $A$ be the coefficient ring and let $T$ be the prime defining the level. For weights $k,l$, write $S_{k,l}(\mathrm{GL}_2(A))$ for the space of Drinfeld cusp forms for $\mathrm{GL}_2(A)$, and $S_{k,l}(\Gamma_0(T))$ for the corresponding space at level $\Gamma_0(T)$. Let $S_{k,l}^{T-\mathrm{old}}(\Gamma_0(T))$ and $S_{k,l}^{T-\mathrm{new}}(\Gamma_0(T))$ denote the $T$-old and $T$-new subspaces, and let $T_T$ and $U_T$ be the relevant Hecke operators. **Bandini–Valentino's conjecture.** (i) The operator $T_T$ acting on $S_{k,l}(\mathrm{GL}_2(A))$ has trivial kernel, (ii) 

$$
S_{k,l}(\Gamma_0(T))=S_{k,l}^{T-\mathrm{old}}(\Gamma_0(T))\oplus S_{k,l}^{T-\mathrm{new}}(\Gamma_0(T)),
$$

and (iii) $U_T$ is diagonalizable on $S_{k,l}(\Gamma_0(T))$. The conjecture would establish the expected oldform–newform decomposition and diagonalizability of the $U_T$-operator for Drinfeld modular forms at this prime level; the supplied text gives no resolution status.

D32.title: Gouvêa–Mazur conjecture on local constancy of slopes
D32.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime number, let $N$ be a positive integer coprime to $p$, and normalize the $p$-adic valuation on $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_p$ by $v_p(p)=1$. For $r\in\mathbb{Q}$ and a space $S$ of modular forms with $U_p$-action, let $d(S,r)$ be the number of generalized eigenvalues of $U_p$ with $p$-adic valuation $r$. Let $S_k(\Gamma_0(Np))$ be the space of cusp forms of weight $k$ and level $Np$. **Gouvêa–Mazur conjecture.** The polynomial $M(x)$ in the preceding local-constancy statement can be chosen as $M(x)=x$; equivalently, for every $r\in\mathbb{Q}_{\geq 0}$, if $k_1,k_2$ are integers satisfying

$$
k_1\geq 2r+2,\qquad k_2\geq 2r+2,
$$

and

$$
k_1\equiv k_2\pmod{(p-1)p^m}
$$

for an integer $m\geq r$, then

$$
d\left(S_{k_1}(\Gamma_0(Np)),r\right)=d\left(S_{k_2}(\Gamma_0(Np)),r\right).
$$

The conjecture concerns the local constancy of slopes of modular forms as the weight varies $p$-adically. Buzzard and Calegari disproved it by giving an explicit counterexample, so the claim is refuted.

D32.title: Smoothed weighted one-level density conjecture for the Riemann zeta-function
D32.statement:
Let $N_f(t):=\sum_\gamma f\left((\gamma-t)/(2\pi/\log T)\right)$, where the sum is over the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta-function. Let $k\in\mathbb N$, let $f$ be even with $\hat f\in\mathcal{C}^{\infty}_c(\mathbb R)$, and let $\phi$ be smooth with compact support in $\mathbb R_{>0}$. Define its Mellin transform by

$$
\widetilde\phi(s):=\int_{\mathbb R}\phi(x)x^{s-1}\,dx.
$$

**Smoothed weighted one-level density conjecture.** As $T\to\infty$,

$$
\frac{1}{c_kT(\log T)^{k^2}}\int_{\mathbb R}N_f(t)|\zeta(\tfrac12+it)|^{2k}\phi\left(\frac{t}{T}\right)\,dt=\widetilde\phi(1)\int_{\mathbb R}f(x)W_U^k(x)\,dx+O((\log T)^{-1}).
$$

This is the naturally smoothed version of the weighted one-level density conjecture and is expected to hold for all positive integers $k$; no asymptotic formula is known for the associated moments over zeros when $k>1$.

D32.title: Cancellation-free identity for graded characters of level-zero Demazure submodules in type C
D32.statement:
Let $W$ be the Weyl group of type $C_n$, let $P^+$ be the set of dominant weights, and let $\varepsilon_k$, $\mathcal{A}$, $\Theta_k$, $\Gamma_k(k)$, $\operatorname{gch} V_x^-(\lambda)$, $\operatorname{end}(B)$, $\operatorname{down}(B)$, and $\mathbf{p}_{\overline{m},k}(w)$ have the meanings specified in the paper. For $x=wt_\xi\in W_{\mathrm{af}}$ with $w\in W$ and $\xi\in Q^\vee$, take $m=1,\ldots,n$ and $\lambda\in P^+$ such that $\lambda+\varepsilon_k\in P^+$ for all $k=1,\ldots,n$ and $\lambda-\varepsilon_k\in P^+$ for $k=m+1,\ldots,n$.

**Cancellation-free identity.** There exists some $m\leq l\leq n$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}
 e^{-w\varepsilon_m}\operatorname{gch}V_x^-(\lambda)
={}&q^{-\langle\varepsilon_m,\xi\rangle}\sum_{B\in\mathcal{A}(w,\Theta_m)}(-1)^{|B|}\operatorname{gch}V_{\operatorname{end}(B)t_{\operatorname{down}(B)+\xi}}^-(\lambda-\varepsilon_m)\\
&+\sum_{k=m+1}^n q^{-\langle\varepsilon_k,\operatorname{down}(\mathbf{p}_{\overline m,\overline k}(w))+\xi\rangle}\\
&\quad\times\sum_{B\in\mathcal{A}(\operatorname{end}(\mathbf{p}_{\overline m,\overline k}(w)),\Theta_k)}(-1)^{|B|}\operatorname{gch}V_{\operatorname{end}(B)t_{\operatorname{down}(B)+\operatorname{down}(\mathbf{p}_{\overline m,\overline k}(w))+\xi}}^-(\lambda-\varepsilon_k)\\
&+\sum_{k=1}^l q^{\langle\varepsilon_k,\operatorname{down}(\mathbf{p}_{\overline m,k}(w))+\xi\rangle}\\
&\quad\times\sum_{B\in\mathcal{A}(\operatorname{end}(\mathbf{p}_{\overline m,k}(w)),\Gamma_k(k))}(-1)^{|B|}\operatorname{gch}V_{\operatorname{end}(B)t_{\operatorname{down}(B)+\operatorname{down}(\mathbf{p}_{\overline m,k}(w))+\xi}}^-(\lambda+\varepsilon_k).
\end{aligned}
$$

This is proposed as a cancellation-free inverse Chevalley-type identity for graded characters of level-zero Demazure submodules over quantum affine algebras of type $C$. The supplied text does not indicate whether the conjecture has been proved or disproved.

D32.title: Steel's lightface Levy-hierarchy mouse set conjecture
D32.statement: Assume $ZF + AD + DC + V=L(\mathbb{R})$. A **mouse set** is a set $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ for which there is an $\omega_1+1$-iterable premouse $M$ with $X=M\cap\mathbb{R}$. Let $\Gamma$ be a level of the lightface Levy hierarchy, and let $C_\Gamma$ denote the associated canonical pointset. **Steel's conjecture.** The set $C_\Gamma$ is a mouse set. This asks whether every lightface Levy-hierarchy pointclass has a mouse corresponding exactly to it; the paper reports partial progress, including the case $\Gamma=\Sigma_2(J_2(\mathbb{R}))$, while the general conjecture remains open.

D32.title: MLDE conjecture for twisted characters of DC-series affine vertex algebras
D32.statement:
Let $V$ be a simple affine vertex algebra associated with one of the Lie algebras in the $\mathrm{DC}$ series

$$
A_{1}subset A_{2} subset G_{2} subset D_{4} subset F_{4}subset E_{6} subset E_{7} subset E_{8}
$$

at level $-h^{\vee}/6-1$. Let $\chi^{\mathrm{twi}}(q)$ denote a normalized $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$-twisted character. **MLDE conjecture.** The functions $\chi^{\mathrm{twi}}(q)$ are solutions of a second-order $\Gamma^{0}(2)$-MLDE with suitable coefficients $a_{1}$ and $a_{2}$, without a $D^{(1)}_{q}$ term:

$$
\left(D^{(2)}_{q}+a_{1}\Theta_{0,2}+a_{2}\Theta_{1,1}\right)\chi^{\mathrm{twi}}(q)=0.
$$

This conjecture predicts a uniform second-order modular linear differential equation for normalized characters of the $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$-twisted modules across the DC series; the paper establishes analogous MLDE results in several examples, while the general assertion remains open.

D32.title: The McKay–Thompson moonshine conjecture
D32.statement: Let $g$ be an element of the Monster group, and let $j_g(q)$ be its McKay–Thompson series. For a prime level $N$, let $\Gamma_0(N)$ be the congruence subgroup of the modular group and let $\Gamma_0(N)^+$ denote its normaliser in $SL(2;\mathbb{Z})$. **Moonshine conjecture.** The McKay–Thompson series $j_g(q)$ is the unique modular invariant of a group lying between $\Gamma_0(N)$ and its normaliser $\Gamma_0(N)^+$ in the modular group $SL(2;\mathbb{Z})$. This conjecture is part of monstrous moonshine, which relates the representation theory of the Monster group to modular functions; the supplied passage does not state whether this formulation has been proved.

D32.title: GOE level-spacing conjecture for Liouville quantum gravity
D32.statement:
