Let $\gamma\in(0,2)$, let $\mu_\gamma$ be the Liouville measure on $D$, and let $(\boldsymbol{\lambda}_j)_{j\ge1}$ be the LQG eigenvalues. Write $F_{\mathrm{GOE}}(x)$ for the GOE level-spacing distribution. **GOE spacing conjecture.** For each $x\ge0$,

$$
\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^N 1_{\{c_\gamma\mu_\gamma(D)(\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{j+1}-\boldsymbol{\lambda}_j)\le x\}}
\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{p}F_{\mathrm{GOE}}(x).
$$

The rescaling uses the Weyl-law mean spacing. The conjecture is motivated by the Bohigas–Giannoni–Schmit prediction and is unresolved in the source.

D32.title: The conjectural reciprocity law for rigid meromorphic cocycles
D32.statement:
Fix open subgroups $U^p\subseteq G(\mathbb{A}^{p,\infty})$ and $U_p\subseteq G(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ containing $G(\mathbb{Q}_p)^+$, and put $U=U^pU_pG(\mathbb{R})^+$. For a coset $h\in G(\mathbb{A})/U$, let $\Gamma_h=G(\mathbb{Q})\cap hUh^{-1}$. Let $(\vec{x},h)$ be an oriented adelic special point, let $C_{x,h}$ be its associated relative class group, let $H_{x,h}/E_x$ be the corresponding abelian extension, and let $E_U$ be the field appearing in the source. Write $t\star(\vec{x},h)$ for the class-group action and $\operatorname{rec}:C_{x,h}\to\operatorname{Gal}(H_{x,h}/E_x)$ for the Artin reciprocity map. **Conjectural reciprocity law.** For every rigid meromorphic cocycle $J\in\mathcal{RMC}(\Gamma_h)$ of level $\Gamma_h$, there exists a finitely generated submodule $\Pi_J\subseteq \mathbb{Q}_p^\times$ of rank less than or equal to the rank of $H^s(\Gamma_h,\mathbb{Z})$ such that

$$
J[(\vec{x},h)]\in H_{x,h}E_U\Pi_J
$$

for every oriented special pair $(\vec{x},h)$ at which $J$ is regular. Moreover, for every $\alpha\in\Pi_J$ such that $J[(\vec{x},h)]/\alpha\in H_{x,h}E_U$, there exists $\alpha'\in\Pi_J$ such that

$$
\operatorname{rec}(t)\left(\frac{J[(\vec{x},h)]}{\alpha}\right)=\frac{J[t\star(\vec{x},h)]}{\alpha'}\quad\forall t\in C_{x,h}^{U}.
$$

This is an analogue of Shimura reciprocity: the values of rigid meromorphic cocycles at adelic special pairs should be defined over the predicted class-field-theoretic extensions, up to the finitely generated ambiguity $\Pi_J$, with Galois action compatible with the class-group action. The source presents this as conjectural and gives no resolution.

D32.title: Darmon's Stark–Heegner point conjecture
D32.statement:
Let $f$ be a weight-$2$ newform of level $\Gamma_0(p)$ with integer Fourier coefficients, let $E=E_f$ be the associated elliptic curve with multiplicative reduction at $p$, and let $P_\tau^{\pm}$ be the Stark–Heegner point obtained from the elliptic theta cocycles and Tate uniformisation. Let $\tau\in\Gamma\backslash\mathcal{H}_p^{\operatorname{RM}}$ be a point of discriminant $D$ prime to $p$, and let $H_\tau$ be the narrow ring class field of the order $\mathcal{O}_\tau$ attached to $\tau$. **Darmon's Stark–Heegner point conjecture.** One has

$$
P_\tau^{\pm}\in E(H_\tau).
$$

This conjecture is the real-quadratic analogue of the algebraicity of classical Heegner points and predicts that the $p$-adicly constructed points are defined over the corresponding narrow ring class fields. The source states that it and suitable generalisations have been verified extensively.

D32.title: Sarnak–Xue density hypothesis
D32.statement:
Let $G\leq GL_n$ be a connected semisimple linear algebraic group over $\mathbb{Q}$ with non-compact $G_\infty=G(\mathbb{R})$. For $q\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\Gamma(q)$ be the level-$q$ congruence subgroup, let $\Pi^{\mathrm{unit}}(G_\infty)$ denote the irreducible unitary representations of $G_\infty$, let $r(\pi)\in[2,\infty]$ be the rate of decay of matrix coefficients, and let $m(\pi;q)$ be the multiplicity of $\pi$ in $L^2(\Gamma(q)\backslash G_\infty)$. **Sarnak–Xue density hypothesis.** For any $\pi\in\Pi^{\mathrm{unit}}(G_\infty)$,

$$
m(\pi;q)\ll\operatorname{vol}(\Gamma(q)\backslash G_\infty)^{\frac{2}{r(\pi)}}.
$$

This is the classical density hypothesis relating multiplicities in congruence quotients to the decay of matrix coefficients; its status is not specified in the source.

D32.title: $p$-adic cohomological Sarnak–Xue density hypothesis
D32.statement:
Let $G$ be a definite Gross inner form of $SO_5$ over a number field, let $p$ be a prime of the number field, let $G_p=G(\mathbb{Q}_p)$, let $\Gamma_p(q)$ be the level-$q$ $p$-arithmetic subgroup, let $\Pi(G_p)$ be the irreducible admissible representations of $G_p$, and let $r(\pi)$ and $m(\pi;q)$ denote the rate of decay of matrix coefficients and the multiplicity in $L^2(\Gamma_p(q)\backslash G_p)$, respectively. **$p$-adic cohomological Sarnak–Xue density hypothesis.** For any $\pi\in\Pi(G_p)$,

$$
m(\pi;q)\ll\operatorname{vol}(\Gamma_p(q)\backslash G_p)^{\frac{2}{r(\pi)}}.
$$

This is the proposed $p$-adic analogue for definite Gross inner forms; the source does not state whether it is resolved.

D32.title: Powerlessness conjecture for late changepoint detection below the square-root scale
D32.statement:
Consider the preferential attachment model with changepoint time $\tau_n=n-cn^\gamma$ for $c>0$ and $\gamma\in(0,1)$, and let $D_v(n)$ denote the degree of vertex $v$ in the final network and $G_n$ the final network snapshot. A test is **powerful** if its power tends to one while its type-I error tends to zero.

**Powerlessness conjecture.** When $\gamma<\tfrac{1}{2}$, all tests based on the vertex degrees $\{D_v(n)\}_{v\in[n]}$ are powerless, and all tests based on $G_n$ are powerless.

The second assertion is stronger because it rules out using higher-level information in the edge structure of $G_n$. The question is formally open; the conjecture is motivated by the fact that degree-count mean shifts are of order $n^\gamma$, below their fluctuation scale when $\gamma<\tfrac{1}{2}$, and by asymptotic normality results suggesting that the corresponding distributions have vanishing total variation distance.

D32.title: Spectral fourth moment conjecture for weight 1 Maass forms
D32.statement:
Let $N$ be the level, and let $\{\mu_j^1\}_j$ be an orthonormal basis of Maass forms of weight $1$ on $\Gamma_0(N)$, with spectral parameters $t_j$ and Fourier coefficients $\rho_j^1(1)$. Fix $r\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\epsilon>0$. **Spectral fourth moment conjecture for weight $1$ Maass forms.** As $T\to\infty$, one has

$$
\sum_{\lvert t_j\rvert\leq T}\frac{\lvert\rho_j^1(1)\rvert^2}{\cosh(\pi t_j)}\left\lvert L\left(\tfrac12+ir,\mu_j^1\right)\right\rvert^4\ll_{N,r,\epsilon}T^{1+\epsilon}.
$$

This conjectural fourth-moment estimate would extend the well-understood spectral fourth-moment bounds for weight $0$ Maass forms to weight $1$ and, through raising and lowering operators, to other odd weights. Such estimates are intended to control the discrete-spectrum contribution in shifted-convolution Dirichlet series and are presented as unavailable in the existing literature.

D32.title: Conjecture on finitely many vanishing quadratic twists for higher-weight modular forms
D32.statement:
Let $f$ be a newform of level $\Gamma_0(N)$ and even weight $k$ with $k\geq 6$, let $\pi$ be the cuspidal automorphic representation of $\operatorname{PGL}_2(\mathbb{A})$ generated by $f$, and let $\varepsilon(\frac{1}{2},\pi\otimes\eta_E)$ denote the root number associated with the twist by the quadratic character $\eta_E$ of a quadratic field $E$. **Finiteness conjecture.** There are at most finitely many quadratic fields $E$ such that

$$
\varepsilon\left(\frac{1}{2},\pi\otimes\eta_E\right)=1
\quad\text{and}\quad
L\left(\frac{1}{2},\pi\otimes\eta_E\right)=0.
$$

The assertion strengthens the expected scarcity of central-value vanishings for even-weight modular forms of weight at least $6$. It is explicitly described as still open, and the source notes that not even examples of modular forms satisfying it are known.

D32.title: The possibility of non-square congruence subgroups for linear level polynomials
D32.statement:
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be such that $\alpha\neq 0$, and consider the congruence subgroups $\Gamma_1(\alpha T+\beta)$ and $\Gamma_0(\alpha T+\beta)$. A congruence subgroup is called **non-square** when it does not satisfy the paper's notion of being square.

**Non-square congruence subgroup conjecture.** Both $\Gamma_1(\alpha T+\beta)$ and $\Gamma_0(\alpha T+\beta)$ may be non-square congruence subgroups for any choice of $\alpha\neq 0$ and $\beta$.

The claim concerns the stabilizers of elliptic points and is used to determine the relevant geometric invariants of the associated Drinfeld modular curves. The supplied context does not state whether this possibility has been established or remains open.

D32.title: Unreachability below $\bf{\Delta^1_3}$
D32.statement: Let $\bf{\Gamma}$ be a pointclass, and let $\kappa$ be $\bf{\Gamma}$-reachable when there is a sequence of distinct $\bf{\Gamma}$-sets of length $\kappa$; otherwise, $\kappa$ is $\bf{\Gamma}$-unreachable. Write $\bf{\Gamma}<_w\bf{\Delta^1_3}$ for the weak ordering of pointclasses used in the source. **Unreachability conjecture.** There is no pointclass $\bf{\Gamma}<_w\bf{\Delta^1_3}$ such that $\aleph_{\omega+1}$ is $\bf{\Gamma}$-reachable. The question is part of the paper's open problems on unreachability; analogous questions at higher projective levels are also left open.

D32.title: Ordering conjecture for multiplying bifurcations of the symmetric periodic orbit
D32.statement:
Let $\Gamma^{*}$ be the single-loop $R^{*}$-symmetric periodic orbit in the zero-energy level, with nontrivial Floquet multipliers $\xi_{\pm}$, and let $\beta_2$ denote the system parameter. Write $\mathbf{{B}_{k}}$ for the period-$k$ multiplying bifurcations and $\mathbf{{\widehat{B}}_{k}}$ for the symmetry-breaking period-$k$ multiplying bifurcations. The symbols $R_{1}$ and $R_{2}$ denote the relevant symmetries of the bifurcating orbits; $\mathbf{{T}_{3}}$, $\mathbf{SN}$ and $\mathbf{HH}$ denote, respectively, the transcritical-type triple-loop bifurcation, the saddle-node point and the Hamiltonian-Hopf bifurcation.

**Ordering conjecture.**

1. The period-$k$ multiplying bifurcations $\mathbf{{B}_{k}}$ occur at the values of $\beta_2$ where

$$
\xi_{\pm}=e^{\pm 2\pi\frac{k-2}{k}}
$$

for all odd $k\geq1$.

2. The symmetry-breaking period-$k$ multiplying bifurcations $\mathbf{{\widehat{B}}_{k}}$ occur at the values of $\beta_2$ where

$$
\xi_{\pm}=e^{\pm 2\pi\frac{k-1}{k}}
$$

for all odd $k\geq1$.

3. The corresponding bifurcating $R^{*}$-symmetric, $R_{1}$-symmetric and $R_{2}$-symmetric $k$-loop orbits exist below and up the respective $\beta_2$-value, except for the transcritical-type case $\mathbf{{B}_{3}}=\mathbf{{T}_{3}}$, where the triple-loop orbits exist up to $\mathbf{SN}$ at $\beta_2\approx0.649089$.

4. Since $\frac{k-2}{k}$ and $\frac{k-1}{k}$ tend to $1$ as $k\to\infty$, both sequences $\mathbf{{B}_{k}}$ and $\mathbf{{\widehat{B}}_{k}}$ approach $\mathbf{HH}$ and hence the associated value $\beta_2\approx0.8164$.

D32.title: Existence of a knot with distinct minimum and maximum thin-position heights
D32.statement:
Let $K$ be a knot. For a thin position $\gamma$ of $K$, let $ht(\gamma)$ be the number of thick level spheres, and define $ht(K)$ and $ht_{\min}(K)$ to be the maximum and minimum, respectively, of $ht(\gamma)$ over all thin positions of $K$.

**Height variation conjecture.** There is a knot $K$ such that

$$
ht_{\min}(K)<ht(K).
$$

This conjecture asks whether a knot can have thin positions with different numbers of thick level spheres. The source provides no resolution, so the problem remains open.

D32.title: Feigin–Frenkel duality conjecture for regular W-superalgebras
D32.statement:
Let $n,r\geq0$, let $\mathcal{W}^k(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+r|n},f_{n+r|n})$ be the universal regular W-superalgebra, let $\mathrm{SB}^{p|q}=\beta\gamma^{\otimes p}\otimes bc^{\otimes q}$, and let $V_{\mathbb{Z}^n}$ be the rank-$n$ lattice vertex algebra. **W-superalgebra duality and rationality conjecture.** For generic levels $k,\ell$ satisfying

$$
(k+r)(\ell+n+r)=1,
$$

there is an isomorphism

$$
\mathcal{W}^k(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+r|n},f_{n+r|n})\simeq\begin{cases}\operatorname{Com}\left(V^{\ell+r}(\mathfrak{gl}_n),\mathcal{W}^{\ell}(\mathfrak{sl}_{n+r},f_{1^n,r})\otimes V_{\mathbb{Z}^n}\right),&r\geq1,\\operatorname{Com}\left(V^{\ell}(\mathfrak{gl}_n),V^{\ell}(\mathfrak{sl}_n)\otimes\beta\gamma^{\otimes n}\otimes V_{\mathbb{Z}^n}\right),&r=0.\end{cases}
$$

Moreover, the regular W-superalgebras are rational and $C_2$-cofinite at levels $k=-r+r/p$ with $p\geq n+r$ and $r>n$. The conjecture connects resolved-conifold boundary-condition duality with rationality of regular W-superalgebras.

D32.title: The arithmetic transfer conjecture for odd type $(r,0)$
D32.statement:
Let $r$ be odd with $0\leq r\leq n$, and let $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^{[r]}_n$ be the formal scheme defined by the Cartesian construction above, with arithmetic intersection number

$$
\left\langle {\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^{[r]}_{n}},g{\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^{[r]}_{n}}\right\rangle_{\mathcal{N}^{[r]}_{n}\times\mathcal{N}_{n+1}}.
$$

**Arithmetic transfer conjecture for odd type $(r,0)$.** There exists $\varphi'\in C_c^\infty(G')$ transferring to $(c_r^2\\,\mathbf{1}_{K_n^{[r]}\times K_{n+1}},0)$ such that, for every matched pair $\gamma\in G'(F_0)_{\mathrm{rs}}$ and $g\in G_{W_1}(F_0)_{\mathrm{rs}}$,

$$
\left\langle {\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^{[r]}_{n}},g{\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}^{[r]}_{n}}\right\rangle_{\mathcal{N}^{[r]}_{n}\times\mathcal{N}_{n+1}}\log q=-\frac12\operatorname{\partial Orb}(\gamma,\varphi').
$$

Moreover, every such transfer admits a correction function $\varphi'_{\mathrm{corr}}$ giving the corresponding identity with the additional term $-\operatorname{Orb}(\gamma,\varphi'_{\mathrm{corr}})$. This is open beyond the cases discussed in the paper; the density conjecture is stated to imply the correction-function formulation from the first part.

D32.title: The Gorenstein contraction conjecture for multiscale differentials
D32.statement:
Let $(X,\eta)$ be a generalized multiscale differential with semistable modification $(\tilde{X},\tilde{\eta})$, dual graph $\tilde{\Gamma}$, levels indexed by $i$, and vanishing orders $\tilde{\ell}_i$ at those levels. Let $\tilde{X}_{>i}$ denote the union of components above level $i$, and let $\mathcal H(\mu)$ be the stratum of holomorphic differentials with zero multiplicities prescribed by $\mu$. **Gorenstein contraction conjecture.** (i) Suppose $(\tilde{X},\tilde{\eta})$ arises as the limit of a one-parameter family $\tilde{\mathcal C}$ of holomorphic differentials $(C_t,\omega_t)$ in $\mathcal H(\mu)$ as $t$ approaches zero. Then, for every level $i$ above all leaf vertices in $\tilde{\Gamma}$, there exists a reduced Gorenstein contraction $\sigma\colon\tilde{\mathcal C}\to\mathcal C'$ contracting exactly $\tilde{X}_{>i}$, such that $\tilde{\eta}_i$ descends to a local generator of $\omega_{X'}$, where $X'$ is the central fiber of $\mathcal C'$ and has isolated Gorenstein singularities formed by contracting each connected component of $\tilde{X}_{>i}$. Moreover, 
$$
\sigma^{*}\omega_{\mathcal C'}=\omega_{\tilde{\mathcal C}}\bigg(\sum_{j>i}(\tilde{\ell}_i-\tilde{\ell}_j)\tilde{X}_j\bigg).
$$
 (ii) Conversely, if for every level $i$ there exists a contraction $\varsigma\colon\tilde{X}\to X'$ contracting each connected component of $\tilde{X}_{>i}$ to an isolated singularity of $X'$ and $\tilde{\eta}_i$ descends to a local section of $\omega_{X'}$ at the resulting singularities, then $(X,\eta)$ can be smoothed into $\mathcal H(\mu)$. This conjecture characterizes smoothability of generalized multiscale differentials through compatible Gorenstein contractions of components above each level; the stated equivalence between one-parameter smoothings and such contractions remains unresolved here.

D32.title: Level-aspect Bergman-kernel size conjecture for Siegel cusp forms
D32.statement:
Let $n\geq 1$, let $\Gamma\subset\operatorname{Sp}_n(\mathbf Z)$ be a congruence subgroup of level $N$, and let $S^{(n)}_k(\Gamma)$ and $\mathbb B_{k,\Gamma}(Z)$ be as above. **Level-aspect Bergman-kernel size conjecture.** With $k$ fixed, as the level $N$ of $\Gamma$ tends to infinity,

$$
\sup_{Z\in\mathbf H_n}\mathbb B_{k,\Gamma}(Z)\asymp_{n,k}1.
$$

This is the proposed correct $L^2$-size in the level aspect. The paper explains that lower bounds are available and that a hybrid asymptotic would be desirable, but the conjectured upper and lower comparison in the general non-compact arithmetic setting remains open.

D32.title: Level-aspect sup-norm conjecture for Siegel Hecke eigenforms
D32.statement:
Let $F$ be as in the preceding individual-eigenform conjecture, let $\Gamma=\Gamma_0^{(n)}(N)$, and define

$$
\lVert F\rVert_\infty:=\sup_{Z=X+iY\in\mathbf H_n}\det(Y)^{k/2}|F(Z)|.
$$

**Level-aspect sup-norm conjecture.** With $F$ and $\Gamma$ as above, as $N\to\infty$,

$$
\lVert F\rVert_\infty\ll_k N^{-n(n+1)/4}.
$$

This is the expected individual-eigenform bound in the level aspect for $\Gamma_0^{(n)}(N)$. It is presented as a conjectural strengthening beyond what follows from the average Bergman-kernel estimates and remains open in the stated generality.

D32.title: The distributional conjecture for normalized L-invariants
D32.statement:
Let $N$ be an integer coprime to $p$, set $\Gamma_0=\Gamma_0(Np)$, and let $\overline{\rho}:\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb Q}/\mathbb Q)\to\operatorname{GL}_2(\overline{\mathbb F}_p)$ be modular of level $\Gamma_0(N)$. Let $S_k(\Gamma_0)^{\pm}$ be the subspace of $p$-new cuspforms on which $a_p=\pm p^{k/2-1}$. For each sign, define

$$
\mathbf y_T^{\pm}(\overline{\rho})=\left\{\frac{2(p+1)}{k(p-1)}v_p(\mathcal L_f)\ \middle|\ f\in S_k(\Gamma_0)^{\pm}\text{ is an eigenform of weight }k\le T,\ \overline{\rho}_f\simeq\overline{\rho}\right\}.
$$

**Distributional conjecture.** For each sign $\pm$, the sets $\mathbf y_T^{\pm}(\overline{\rho})$ become equidistributed for Lebesgue measure on $[-1,0]$ as $T\to\infty$.
This conjecture proposes a statistical law for $p$-adic valuations of $\mathcal L$-invariants and is presented as a close relative of Gouvêa's slope distribution conjecture. The paper supplies numerical and heuristic evidence but no proof of the general statement.

D32.title: Miura's second-energy conjecture for the elastic propeller
D32.statement:
For a tame knot class $K$, let $\mathcal{K}$ be the $W^{2,2}$-closure of the class of unit-length, arclength-parametrized closed curves in $K$:

$$
\mathcal{K}:=\overline{\{\gamma\in W^{2,2}(\mathbf{R}/\mathbf{Z};\mathbf{R}^3)\mid |\gamma'|\equiv1,\ \gamma\in K\}}.
$$

A **stable elastic knot** for $K$ is a curve $\gamma\in\mathcal{K}$ that locally minimizes the bending energy $B$ on a connected component of the knot class, and it is **strictly stable** if the minimum is strict up to isometry. **Elastic propeller conjecture.** The elastic propeller is a strictly stable elastic knot for the unknot class. Moreover, among all stable elastic knots for the unknot class, it has the second smallest energy. The circle is the least-energy stable elastic unknot, so the conjecture identifies the elastic propeller as the next energy level. The source attributes this conjecture to Miura; its resolution is not specified.

D32.title: Generalized Billerey-Menares conjecture for squarefree levels
D32.statement:
Let $k\geq 4$ and let $\ell>k+1$ be prime. Let $N=p_1\cdots p_t$ be squarefree, with distinct prime factors $p_i$, and let $\varepsilon$ be an Atkin-Lehner eigensystem for $\Gamma_0(N)$, meaning a multiplicative function on the positive divisors of $N$ with values in $\{\pm1\}$ and value $1$ at $1$. Let $\mathcal{S}_k^{(\varepsilon)}(N)$ denote the subspace of cusp forms in which the Atkin-Lehner operator $W_p$ has eigenvalue $\varepsilon(p)$ for every $p\mid N$. **Generalized Billerey-Menares conjecture.** The following are equivalent:

1. $\ell \mid \dfrac{B_k}{2k}\prod_{i=1}^{t}(1+\varepsilon(p_i)p_i^{k/2})$ and, for every $1\leq i\leq t$, $\ell\mid (1+\varepsilon(p_i)p_i^{k/2})(1+\varepsilon(p_i)p_i^{k/2-1})$.
2. There exist a newform $f\in\mathcal{S}_k^{(\varepsilon)}(N)$ and a prime ideal $\Lambda$ over $\ell$ in the coefficient field of $f$ such that

$$
\overline{\rho}_{f,\Lambda}\simeq 1\oplus\overline{\chi}_\ell^{k-1}.
$$

This refines the conjecture of Billerey and Menares on non-optimal squarefree levels of $1\oplus\overline{\chi}_\ell^{k-1}$ by incorporating Atkin-Lehner eigensystems; the source provides no resolution status.

D32.title: Gross–Kudla conjecture on triple-product L-functions and Bloch–Beilinson heights
D32.statement:
Let $f,g,h$ be weight $2$ cusp forms of level $\Gamma_{0}(N)$, where $N$ is squarefree, and set $F=f\times g\times h$ on $\mathbb{H}^{3}$. Let $X$ be the canonically defined Shimura curve associated with this setting, let $\Gamma^{3}$ be its modified diagonal cycle, let $\Gamma^{3}_{F}$ denote the $F$-isotypic component of $\Gamma^{3}$, and let $\langle\,\ \rangle_{\mathrm{BB}}$ be the Bloch–Beilinson height pairing. Write $L(F,s)$ for the associated triple-product $L$-function, centered at $s=2$.

**Gross–Kudla conjecture.**

$$
L'(F,2)=\Omega(F)\langle\Gamma^{3}_{F},\Gamma^{3}_{F}\rangle_{\mathrm{BB}},
$$

where $\Omega(F)$ is an explicit non-zero constant.

This conjecture relates the central derivative of a triple-product $L$-function to the Bloch–Beilinson height of a modified diagonal cycle. The supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or disproved.

D32.title: Bean's informal high-dimensional asymptotics for the full conformal LASSO
D32.statement:
Let $(X_i,Y_i)_{i=1}^{n+1}$ follow the data-generating process described in Section 2, let $\hat{\beta}$ be the LASSO estimator fit on all $n+1$ observations, and let $\hat{\beta}_{(n+1)}$ be the corresponding estimator fit on the first $n$ observations. Let $\lambda_i$ and $\epsilon_i$ denote the scale and noise variables, let $\beta_i^*$ denote the population regression coefficients, and suppose that $d/n\to\gamma$. **Bean's informal asymptotic conjecture.** Under these assumptions, there exist asymptotic constants $N_{\infty}$ and $c_{\infty}$ such that

$$
Y_i-X_i^\top\hat{\beta}-\frac{1}{1+2\lambda_{n+1}^2c_{\infty}}(Y_{n+1}-X_{n+1}^\top\hat{\beta}_{(n+1)})\stackrel{\mathbb{P}}{\to}0,
$$

and

$$
\|\hat{\beta}-\hat{\beta}_{(n+1)}\|_2\stackrel{\mathbb{P}}{\to}N_{\infty}.
$$

Moreover, $N_{\infty}$ and $c_{\infty}$ can be computed exactly as solutions of a system of equations depending only on the distributions of $\epsilon_i$, $\lambda_i$, and $\beta_i^*$, the regularization level $\tau$, and the ratio $\gamma$. These asymptotics are heuristic and supported by simulations rather than proved in the paper; they are intended to predict the high-dimensional behaviour of the fitted residuals and coefficients underlying full conformal LASSO inference.

D32.title: Stopple's Z-curve conjecture for zeros of the zeta derivative
D32.statement:
Let a **Z-curve** be one of the level curves described in the source for $\zeta'(s)$, and classify zeros of $\zeta'(s)$ by types $0$, $1$, and $2$. Write a zero as $\rho'=\beta'+i\gamma'$. **Stopple's Z-curve conjecture.** Asymptotically, $100\%$ of the zeros lying on a Z-curve are type $0$ and satisfy $\beta'>1$.

The conjecture concerns zeros of $\zeta'(s)$ far from the critical line and is motivated by the numerical data, in which all but one of the observed Z-curve zeros were type $0$ and all but $17$ had real part greater than $1$. No proof or disproof is given.

D32.title: Conrad–Edixhoven–Stein conjecture for rational torsion on $J_1(p)$
D32.statement:
Let $p\geq 5$ be a prime, and let $X_1(p)$ be the modular curve with Jacobian $J_1(p)$. The **rational cuspidal subgroup** is the subgroup generated by divisor classes given by differences of $\mathbb{Q}$-rational cusps. **Conrad–Edixhoven–Stein conjecture.** The $\mathbb{Q}$-rational torsion subgroup of $J_1(p)$ is generated by differences of $\mathbb{Q}$-rational cusps on $X_1(p)$.

This is the prime-level $\Gamma_1(p)$ case of the question relating rational torsion on modular Jacobians to rational cuspidal classes. The source attributes the conjecture to Conrad, Edixhoven, and Stein and does not state whether it has been resolved.

D32.title: Positive-even-rank dimension conjecture for prime level newforms
D32.statement:
For each prime $p$, let $\operatorname{perdim}(p)$ be the number of weight-$2$ newforms $f$ for $\Gamma_0(p)$ such that $w(f)=-f$ and $L(f,1)=0$. **Positive-even-rank dimension conjecture.** The following two forms are proposed:

1. **Weak form:**

$$
\lim_{p\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{perdim}(p)}{\log p}=0
$$

as $p$ runs through all prime numbers.

2. **Strong form:** $\operatorname{perdim}(p)$ is uniformly bounded as $p$ runs through all prime numbers.

The conjecture is supported by the reported computations and by heuristics involving Galois orbits and analytic ranks; neither form is resolved in the supplied text.

D32.title: Dieulefait–González–Lario congruence conjecture for modular forms of CM type mod \ell
D32.statement:
Let $f(q)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_nq^n\in S_2(\Gamma_0(N))^{\operatorname{new}}$ be a normalized newform of CM type mod $\ell$ by an imaginary quadratic field $K$. A newform has **complex multiplication** by $K$ when its coefficients vanish at primes inert in $K$ (away from its level and the relevant prime). Let $\mathfrak{L}$ be a prime ideal above $\ell$ in the composite of the Fourier number fields of $f$ and a second newform. **Dieulefait–González–Lario conjecture.** There exists a normalized newform $g(q)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty b_nq^n\in S_2(\Gamma_0(M))^{\operatorname{new}}$ with CM by $K$ such that

$$
a_p\equiv b_p\pmod{\mathfrak{L}}
$$

for every prime $p\nmid NM\ell$. The conjecture asks whether every weight-$2$ newform of CM type modulo $\ell$ arises modulo $\mathfrak{L}$ from a genuine CM newform; the paper proves the assertion for $\ell>2$, $\ell\neq3$, when $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$, while the general case remains open.

D32.title: The Harris–Venkatesh conjecture for weight-one newforms
D32.statement:
Let $f=\sum_n a_nq^n$ be a newform of weight $1$ and level $\Gamma_1(N)$. Let $\rho_f$ be its Deligne–Serre representation, let ${\mathrm{Ad}}(\rho_f)$ be the trace-free adjoint representation, and let

$$
\mathcal{U}({\mathrm{Ad}}(\rho_f))={\mathrm{Hom}}_{{\mathrm{Gal}}(E/\mathbb{Q})}({\mathrm{Ad}}(\rho_f),\mathcal{O}_E^\times\otimes\mathbb{Z}[f])
$$

be its associated dual space of units. For each prime $p\nmid 6N$, write ${\mathrm{Reg}}_{(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^\times}$ for the $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^\times$-regulator and $\lVert f\rVert^2_{(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^\times}$ for the Harris–Venkatesh norm. **The Harris–Venkatesh conjecture.** There exist $u\in\mathcal{U}({\mathrm{Ad}}(\rho_f))\otimes\mathbb{Q}$ and a prime $p_0$ such that, for all primes $p\geq p_0$,

$$
\lVert f\rVert^2_{(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^\times}={\mathrm{Reg}}_{(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^\times}(u).
$$

Equivalently, the Serre-duality pairing with the derived Hecke operator satisfies

$$
\left\langle f^*,T_{\mathbb{Z}_p,N}(f)\right\rangle_{\mathrm{SD}}={\mathrm{Reg}}_{(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^\times}(u).
$$

This conjecture relates the modulo-$p$ derived Hecke action on weight-one forms to Stark-type units and regulators; the supplied text gives no evidence that it has been resolved.

D32.title: Commutativity of the truncated category O and KLR Grothendieck-group diagram
D32.statement:
Suppose $\mathfrak{g}$ is simply-laced, let $\lambda\in P_+$, let $\mu\in \operatorname{wt}(V(\lambda))$, and choose an integral set of parameters $\mathbf{R}$ of level $\lambda$. Consider the top quotient $(\mathcal O_\mu^\lambda(\mathbf{R}))_{\operatorname{top}}$, the top Borel–Moore homology group of the repelling affine-Grassmannian slice, the KLR Grothendieck group, and the maps $\psi_\lambda$, $\operatorname{CC}_{\operatorname{top}}^{\tilde X_-}$, $\Theta_{\operatorname{cyc}}$, $\gamma$, and ${\Dbar}^{-}$ shown in the source diagram. **Top-level commutativity conjecture.** The diagram 
$$
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=1.5em] \operatorname{H}_{\operatorname{top}}\big((\overline{\mathcal{W}}{}^\lambda_\mu)_-\big)\arrow[dr,"\psi_\lambda"'] & K_0((\mathcal O_\mu^\lambda(\mathbf{R}))_{\operatorname{top}}) \arrow[l,"\operatorname{CC}_{\operatorname{top}}^{\tilde{X}_-}"'] \arrow[r,"\Theta_{\operatorname{cyc}}"] & K_0(R_{\lambda-\mu}^\lambda\,\text{-}\,\operatorname{mod})\arrow[dl,"\gamma"]\\ & {\mathbb C}[N]_{-(\lambda-\mu)} & \end{tikzcd}
$$
 is commutative. This extends the main theorem's commutative diagram after passing to the top quotient; the source presents it as an expected extension, and no resolution is stated.

D32.title: The non-CM Fourier coefficient conjecture for odd discriminant level
D32.statement:
Let $k$ be an integer with $k\geq 3$, and let $D=p_1\cdots p_\ell$ be an odd discriminant. Let $S_k^{\mathrm{Ell}}(\Gamma_1(D),\omega_{E/\mathbb{Q}})$ denote the space of elliptic cusp forms of weight $k$, level $\Gamma_1(D)$, and nebentypus $\omega_{E/\mathbb{Q}}$. A normalized newform in this space is **non-CM** if it does not have complex multiplication. **The non-CM Fourier coefficient conjecture.** If this space contains a non-CM normalized newform, then at least one such newform $f$ satisfies

$$
a_f(p_i)\neq \pm p_i^{(k-1)/2}\quad\text{for every }i.
$$

Here $a_f(p_i)$ is the $p_i$-th Fourier coefficient of $f$. This conjecture asserts that, among the available non-CM newforms, one can find a form avoiding the CM-type extremal values at every prime dividing the odd discriminant. The source provides no resolution, so the conjecture is recorded as open.

D32.title: Buzzard's slope conjecture for modular forms
D32.statement: Let $p>3$ and $N$ be as above, and suppose that $p$ is **$\Gamma_0(N)$-regular**, meaning that the conditions on the eigenvalues of $T_p$ in weights up to $k_p$ hold as specified above. Let $s_2,s_4,\ldots$ be the integer sequences produced by Buzzard's algorithm, and let $v_2,v_4,\ldots$ denote the sequences of $p$-adic valuations of the eigenvalues of $T_p$ acting on $S_k(\Gamma_0(N))$. **Buzzard's slope conjecture.** Assume that $p$ is $\Gamma_0(N)$-regular. Then the sequences $s_2,s_4,\ldots$ of integers are precisely the sequences $v_2,v_4,\ldots$ of $p$-adic valuations of $T_p$ acting on $S_k(\Gamma_0(N))$. This conjecture predicts that Buzzard's combinatorial algorithm exactly determines the $p$-adic slopes of modular forms of fixed level and varying even weight; the source gives no resolution status for this statement.

D32.title: The fundamental local equivalence conjecture for principal equivariant W-algebras
D32.statement:
Let $G$ be a reductive group with maximal torus $T$, coweight lattice $X_{*}(T)$, dominant coweights $X_{*}(T)_{+}$, Langlands dual group $\check{G}$, and principal equivariant affine $\mathcal{W}$-algebra $\mathcal{W}_{G}^{\kappa}$ at level $\kappa$. Let $\mathcal{D}_{G}^{\kappa}$ be the corresponding vertex algebra module, let $H^{*}_{DS}$ denote principal quantum Hamiltonian reduction, and let $\mathcal{W}_{G}^{\kappa}\mathrm{-Mod}^{\mathcal{J}_{\infty}G}$ be the full subcategory of $\mathcal{W}_{G}^{\kappa}$-modules integrable with respect to $\mathcal{J}_{\infty}G$. For each $\gamma\in X_{*}(T)_{+}$, write $\gamma\cdot\mathcal{D}_{G}^{\kappa}$ for the corresponding spectral-flow twist, and let $V_{\gamma}$ be the simple $\check{G}$-module of highest weight $\gamma$. **The fundamental local equivalence conjecture.** For generic levels, the category $\mathcal{W}_{G}^{\kappa}\mathrm{-Mod}^{\mathcal{J}_{\infty}G}$ is semisimple, with simple objects $H^{*}_{DS}(\gamma\cdot\mathcal{D}_{G}^{\kappa})$ for $\gamma\in X_{*}(T)_{+}$. In particular, there is an equivalence of abelian categories

$$
\mathcal{W}_{G}^{\kappa}\mathrm{-Mod}^{\mathcal{J}_{\infty}G}\simeq\check{G}\mathrm{-Mod}
$$

that sends $H^{*}_{DS}(\gamma\cdot\mathcal{D}_{G}^{\kappa})$ to $V_{\gamma}$ for every $\gamma\in X_{*}(T)_{+}$. This is an abelian-category formulation of the fundamental local equivalence in the quantum geometric Langlands program, identifying the representation theory of the principal equivariant $\mathcal{W}$-algebra at generic level with representations of the Langlands dual group. The conjecture remains unproved in the supplied text.

D32.title: Level-two congruence subgroup conjecture for non-spherical small Coxeter groups
D32.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a non-spherical small Coxeter graph, with associated Artin group $A[\Gamma]$, Coxeter group $W[\Gamma]$, and level-two congruence subgroup $A[\Gamma][2]$. Write $W[\Gamma][2]$ for the level-two congruence subgroup of $W[\Gamma]$. **Level-two congruence subgroup conjecture.**

$$
A[\Gamma][2]=\ker\bigl(A[\Gamma]\to W[\Gamma]/W[\Gamma][2]\bigr).
$$

The preceding argument establishes the inclusion of the right-hand kernel in $A[\Gamma][2]$; the conjecture asserts equality for every non-spherical small Coxeter graph. The parser provides no evidence of a resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

D32.title: Ivanov's conjecture on finite-index subgroups of mapping class groups
D32.statement: Let $S_g^n$ be a compact oriented surface of genus $g$ with $n$ boundary components, and let $\mathrm{Mod}(S_g^n)$ be its mapping class group. Let $\Gamma\subset\mathrm{Mod}(S_g^n)$ be a finite-index subgroup, and write $\Gamma^{\mathrm{ab}}$ for its abelianization and $H^1(\Gamma,\mathbb{Z})$ for its first integral cohomology. **Ivanov's conjecture.** For $g\geq 3$ and $n\geq 0$, $\Gamma^{\mathrm{ab}}=H^1(\Gamma,\mathbb{Z})$ is finite. This is a central finite-abelianization conjecture for finite-index subgroups of mapping class groups. The paper notes substantial partial results and the relation to the Putman–Wieland conjecture, but does not state a resolution in the supplied text.

D32.title: Emerton's equidimensionality conjecture for the big Hecke algebra
D32.statement:
Let $p\geq 5$ be an odd prime, let $N\geq 1$ with $p\nmid N$, and let $\mathbb{T}$ be the $p$-adic Hecke algebra defined as the projective limit of the Hecke algebras acting on modular forms of weights at most $k$ and level $\Gamma_1(N)$.

**Emerton's conjecture.** The ring $\mathbb{T}$ is equidimensional of Krull dimension $4$.

This conjecture concerns the dimension of the big Hecke algebra parametrizing systems of Hecke eigenvalues across varying weights. The supplied text proves that $\mathbb{T}$ is $p$-adically complete, Noetherian, and a finite product of Noetherian local $\mathbb{Z}_p$-algebras, but gives no resolution of the equidimensionality claim.

D32.title: Refinement of the Craig–van Ittersum–Ono conjecture for prime-detecting quasimodular forms
D32.statement:
Let $N$ be a positive integer. Let $\beta\widetilde{E}(N)$ denote the space of quasimodular Eisenstein forms on $\Gamma_{0}(N)$, let $\Omega_{N}$ denote the space of prime-detecting quasimodular forms of level $N$, and let $\widetilde{S}^{\mathrm{old}}(N)$ denote the space of quasimodular oldforms on $\Gamma_{0}(N)$. **Refined conjecture.**

$$
\Omega_{N}=\Omega_{N}\cap\left(\widetilde{E}(N)\oplus\widetilde{S}^{\mathrm{old}}(N)\right).
$$

This refinement is motivated by examples whose nonzero cuspidal parts lie in the quasimodular oldform space. It predicts that any failure of the Eisenstein-space inclusion is accounted for by oldforms, while the claim remains open in the source.

D32.title: Critical-level duality conjecture for regular \mathcal{W}-superalgebras
D32.statement:
Assume $n\geqslant m$, and let $\kappa_c$ denote the critical level. Let $\mathcal{A}^m_{\mathrm{deg}}$ be the degenerate $\beta\gamma$-system associated with $\mathbb{C}^m\oplus\overline{\mathbb{C}}^m$, let $\mathcal{F}_{n|m}$ be as above, and let $\mathrm{GL}_m$ act diagonally. **Critical-level duality conjecture.** There is an isomorphism of vertex superalgebras

$$
\mathcal{W}^{\kappa_c}(\mathfrak{gl}_{n|m})\simeq\mathbb{C}[J_\infty\mathbb{A}^{n-m}]\otimes(\mathcal{A}^m_{\mathrm{deg}}\otimes\mathcal{F}_{n|m})^{\mathrm{GL}_m}.
$$

This is the critical-level analogue of Ito's conjectural duality, obtained by interpreting the dual level as $\check{\kappa}=\infty$ and replacing the corresponding $\mathcal{W}$-algebra by the Poisson vertex algebra of functions on the jet scheme of the relevant Slodowy slice.

D32.title: Center conjecture for critical-level regular \mathcal{W}-superalgebras
D32.statement:
Assume $n\geqslant m$, with $\kappa_c$ the critical level, and let $\mathfrak{z}$ denote the commutative center. Let $\mathcal{A}^m_{\mathrm{deg}}$ be the degenerate $\beta\gamma$-system, with its natural $\mathrm{GL}_m$-action. **Center conjecture.** There are isomorphisms of commutative vertex algebras

$$
\mathfrak{z}(V^{\kappa_c}(\mathfrak{gl}_{n|m}))\simeq\mathfrak{z}(\mathcal{W}^{\kappa_c}(\mathfrak{gl}_{n|m}))\simeq\mathbb{C}[J_\infty\mathbb{A}^{n-m}]\otimes(\mathcal{A}^m_{\mathrm{deg}})^{\mathrm{GL}_m}.
$$

The proposed description follows from the critical-level regular $\mathcal{W}$-superalgebra conjecture and is motivated by the corresponding description of centers in the cited work.

D32.title: Deep congruences between twins of newforms
D32.statement: Let $f$ be an admissible newform of weight $k>2$ and level $\Gamma_0(p)$, and suppose that $p$ splits completely in its Hecke field $K_f$. Write $\varepsilon(f)$ for its Atkin--Lehner sign, $\mathcal{L}(f)$ for its $\mathcal{L}$-invariant, and $C_{p,k}$ for the constant in the conjecture. **Deep congruence conjecture.** There exists a unique newform $g$ of weight $k$ and level $\Gamma_0(p)$ such that $\varepsilon(g)=-\varepsilon(f)$, $v_p(\mathcal{L}(f)+\mathcal{L}(g))\ge -C_{p,k}$ (and hence $v_p(\mathcal{L}(f))=v_p(\mathcal{L}(g))$), and the Hecke eigensystems of $f$ and $g$ are congruent modulo $p^{-v_p(\mathcal{L}(f))+1}$. This conjecture predicts a unique opposite-sign twin with unusually deep congruence, supported by the explicit computations in the paper; its general status is open.

D32.title: Calegari--Stein opposite Atkin--Lehner sign conjecture
D32.statement:
Let $k<p-1$, and let $f$ and $g$ be two newforms of level $\Gamma_0(p)$. Write $\varepsilon(f)$ and $\varepsilon(g)$ for their Atkin--Lehner signs, and say that the forms are congruent modulo $p$ when their Hecke eigensystems are congruent modulo $p$. **Calegari--Stein conjecture.** If $f$ and $g$ are congruent modulo $p$, then

$$
\varepsilon(f)=-\varepsilon(g).
$$

The conjecture concerns the relationship between mod-$p$ congruences and Atkin--Lehner signs for weights below $p-1$; the source presents it as an open conjecture compatible with the paper's computations.

D32.title: The global integral-model conjecture for $\Gamma_1(p)$-level Shimura varieties
D32.statement: Assume that $({\mathcal G},\{\mu\})$ is strictly convex, that the divisor conjecture holds, and that an $O_E$-integral model ${\mathcal S}_{K_0}$ of ${\rm Sh}_{K_0}(G,X)_E$ with its local-model morphism $\varphi$ is given. Let $S\subset S_{{\mathcal G},\mu}$ be a semigroup defining $Y_S$ and its Lang cover. **The global $\Gamma_1(p)$-integral-model conjecture.** There exists an $O_E$-integral model ${\mathcal S}_{K_1,S}$ of ${\rm Sh}_{K_1}(G,X)_E$ equipped with a morphism to ${\mathcal S}_{K_0}$ extending the generic-fiber cover, an extended $T_{\mathcal G}(\mathbb F_p)$-action identifying ${\mathcal S}_{K_0}$ with the quotient, the stated prime-to-$p$ equivariance, and a morphism to $[\mathcal G\backslash{\rm M}^{\sqrt S}_{{\mathcal G},\mu}]$ inducing the specified $2$-cartesian quotient-stack isomorphism. This is the proposed systematic construction of integral models at $\Gamma_1(p)$-type level; the source presents it as conjectural and does not claim a general proof.

D32.title: The torus-torsor extension conjecture for $\Gamma_1(p)$-level covers
D32.statement:
Assume the divisor conjecture and let $\pi:{\rm Sh}_{K_1}(G,X)_E%
 \ifbool{@display}{\longrightarrow}{\rightarrow}%
 {\rm Sh}_{K_0}(G,X)_E$ be the generic-fiber $T_{\mathcal G}(\mathbb F_p)$-torsor, represented by a pair $(Q_\pi,a_\pi)$. Let ${\mathcal S}_{K_0}$ be the integral model with local-model morphism $\varphi$. **The torus-torsor extension conjecture.** There exists a $T_{\mathcal G}$-torsor $P$ over ${\mathcal S}_{K_0}$, an isomorphism $P[1/p]\simeq Q_\pi$, and an isomorphism of pairs

$$
\bigl(L_*(P),L_*(\alpha^{-1})\circ a_\pi\bigr)\simeq\varphi^*\bigl({\rm P}^{(-1)}_{{\mathcal G},\mu},s_{{\mathcal G},\mu}\bigr).
$$

This is the proposed torsorial construction underlying the global integral model at $\Gamma_1(p)$-level; it is stated conditionally on the divisor conjecture and is not resolved in the source.

D32.title: The local integral-model conjecture for $\Gamma_1(p)$-level local Shimura varieties
D32.statement: Let $(G,\{\mu\},b)$ be a local Shimura datum, let ${\mathcal G}$ be parahoric, set $K_0={\mathcal G}(\mathbb Z_p)$, and let $K_1$ be the kernel of the reduction map to the reductive abelian quotient over $\mathbb F_p$. Choose $S\subset S_{{\mathcal G},\mu}\subset X^*(T_{\mathcal G})$. **The local $\Gamma_1(p)$-integral-model conjecture.** There exists a formal scheme ${\mathcal M}^{\rm int}_{K_1,S}$ over $\operatorname{Spf}(O_{\breve E})$ with rigid generic fiber ${\rm Sht}_{K_1}(G,\mu,b)$, together with a morphism to ${\mathcal M}^{\rm int}_{K_0}$ extending the generic-fiber cover, an extended $T_{\mathcal G}(\mathbb F_p)$-action identifying the quotient with ${\mathcal M}^{\rm int}_{K_0}$, and a morphism to $[\mathcal G\backslash{\rm M}^{\sqrt S}_{{\mathcal G},\mu}]$ fitting into the stated $2$-commutative diagram and inducing the stated isomorphism of formal stacks. This is the local analogue of the global conjecture; the local-model map is known in at least the PEL case, but the asserted level-$K_1$ formal model is left conjectural.

D32.title: Monotonicity conjecture for new KMP eigenvalues
D32.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a hypergraph with non-negative weights. For every $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, let $\omega_k=\omega_k(\Gamma)$ denote the smallest new eigenvalue of the Laplacian $\mathcal{L}(\Gamma,\mathcal{KMP}_k)$, meaning the smallest eigenvalue arising in the new invariant subspace at level $k$. **Monotonicity conjecture for new KMP eigenvalues.** 

$$
\omega_1\leq\omega_3\leq\omega_5\leq\cdots\qquad\text{and}\qquad\omega_2\leq\omega_4\leq\omega_6\leq\cdots.
$$

The inequalities are supported by computer simulations and generalize the proved result for hypergraphs supported on subsets of size $n-1$. The source gives no resolution in general.

D32.title: Hölder control of diameter by swept-area distance
D32.statement:
Let $K$ be a knot type, let $Y_{\Lambda}(K)$ be the representatives at ropelength level $\Lambda$, and let $d_{\Lambda}^{K}$ be the swept-area pseudometric. For representatives $\gamma_0,\gamma_1$ in the same admissible component, write $\operatorname{diam}(\gamma)$ for the Euclidean diameter of $\gamma$.

**Diameter variation conjecture.** For each ropelength level $\Lambda$, there should exist constants $C(\Lambda)>0$ and $\alpha>0$ such that

$$
|\operatorname{diam}(\gamma_1)-\operatorname{diam}(\gamma_0)| \le C(\Lambda)\\,d_{\Lambda}^{K}(\gamma_0,\gamma_1)^\alpha.
$$

The exponent $\alpha=1/2$ is a natural first candidate. A proof or counterexample would clarify whether diameter and compression radius can provide robust lower bounds for swept-area distance.

D32.title: The combinatorial criterion for kinematic support
D32.statement:
Let $\Gamma_{L^\ast}$ be a graph in the class of loop BCFW graphs $\mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathtt{BCFW}}_{k,n;L^\ast}$, and let

$$
(\mathcal{G}_0,\mathcal{G}_1,\dots,\mathcal{G}_T=\Gamma_{L^\ast})
$$

be the corresponding branch of the loop BCFW recursion. Say that $\Gamma_{L^\ast}$ has **kinematic support** when it satisfies the realizability condition defined in the paper. **Combinatorial criterion for kinematic support.** The graph $\Gamma_{L^\ast}$ has kinematic support if and only if, for all faces $f^\ast,g^\ast$ and all $t=0,1,\dots,T$ for which they are faces of $\mathcal{G}_t$, the faces are $2_{\mathcal{N}}$-separated in $\mathcal{G}_t$ if and only if they are $2_{\mathcal{N}}$-separated in $\mathcal{G}_T=\Gamma_{L^\ast}$. The criterion is presented after an example showing that full $2$-separation alone is not sufficient for kinematic support. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.

D32.title: Bondi mass limits and mass loss for boosted Kerr stability
D32.statement:
Let $(\gamma,k)$ be the initial data from Theorem~, with ADM mass $\mathfrak m_0$ and vanishing linear momentum, let $g$ be the resulting spacetime metric, and set $\chi=\frac12\|\mathsf S\|_{L^\infty}$. Let $M_B$ denote the Bondi mass defined using the level sets of $t_*$ on $\mathscr I^+$, and let $\slashed\pi_0$ and $\slashed g$ denote the asymptotic radiation field and metric. **Bondi mass conjecture.** The Bondi mass of $\phi_\mathsf S^*g$ satisfies

$$
\lim_{t_*\to-\infty}M_B(\phi_\mathsf S^*g;t_*)=\mathfrak m_0,\qquad \lim_{t_*\to+\infty}M_B(\phi_\mathsf S^*g;t_*)=\mathfrak m\cosh\chi,
$$

and obeys

$$
\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm d u}M_B(\phi_\mathsf S^*g;u)=-\frac{1}{32\pi}\int_{\mathscr I^+\cap\{t_*=u\}}\left|r\partial_{t_*}\slashed\pi_0(\phi_\mathsf S^*h)\right|_{\slashed g}^2\,\mathrm d\slashed g.
$$

The conjecture would imply $\mathfrak m\cosh\chi\leq\mathfrak m_0$, expressing that the final Bondi energy cannot exceed the initial energy after accounting for energy carried away by gravitational radiation. Establishing the formula requires higher-order asymptotic computations than those used for nonlinear stability, and the source leaves it open.

D32.title: Badness-level conjecture for Calabi–Yau modular forms
D32.statement:
Let $X$ be a $d$-dimensional Calabi–Yau variety whose associated modular form has weight $d+1$ on some $\Gamma_0(N)$, and write the level as

$$
N=\prod_{p\;\mathrm{bad}}p^{\alpha_p},
$$

where the product is over primes of bad reduction. **Badness-level conjecture.** The exponent $\alpha_p$ increases with the badness of the singularity at the bad prime $p$. This is described as a folklore conjecture motivated by the computed examples; the source gives no general proof or resolution.

D32.title: Ulmer's semisimplicity conjecture for the Hecke operator at level Np
D32.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $N$ be coprime to $p$, and let $S_k(\Gamma_0(Np),\mathbb Q_p)$ be the space of cusp forms of weight $k$ and level $\Gamma_0(Np)$. For a normalized cuspidal eigenform $f\in S_k(N,\mathbb C_p)$, write $a_p$ for the eigenvalue of the Hecke operator $\mathrm{T}_p$ acting on $f$.

**Ulmer's conjecture.** The action of $U_p$ on $S_k(\Gamma_0(Np),\mathbb Q_p)$ is semisimple. In particular, the polynomial

$$
x^2-a_p x+p^{k-1}
$$

always has distinct roots.

This conjecture concerns the diagonalizability of the $U_p$ operator on oldforms and would ensure that the two associated $U_p$-eigenforms have well-defined, separately determined slopes. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture is recorded as open.

D32.title: Buzzard's classical 2-adic Newton polygon conjecture for level-1 cusp forms
D32.statement:
Let $k\geq12$ be even, let $S_k=S_k(\Gamma_0(1),\mathbf{Q})$ be the space of level-$1$ cusp forms of weight $k$, and let $m=\dim S_k$. For a polynomial with rational coefficients, its 2-adic Newton polygon means its Newton polygon over the 2-adic numbers. **Buzzard's classical slope conjecture.** The 2-adic Newton polygon of

$$
\operatorname{det}(1-XT_2)
$$

on $S_k$ equals the 2-adic Newton polygon of

$$
1+\sum_{n=1}^{m}X^n\prod_{j=1}^{n}\frac{2^{2j}(k-8j)!(k-8j-3)!(k-12j-2)}{(k-12j)!(k-6j-1)!}.
$$

The conjecture was verified numerically for all $k\leq2048$ in the source. Via Coleman's control theorems, it is related to the slopes of finite-slope overconvergent cusp forms at tame level $1$; its general validity remains open.

D32.title: Conjecture on the minus Drinfeld–Sokolov reduction of category O modules
D32.statement:
Let $\bar{\ta{ g}}$ be the finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra underlying the affine algebra, let $\bar{\rho}$ be its Weyl vector, let $\bar{\ta{ h}}^*$ be the corresponding finite-dimensional weight space, and let $\bar{\ta{ Delta}}_+$ be the set of positive finite roots. For a level $\tau\ta{ kappa}$, write $\ta{ O}_{\tau\ta{ kappa}}$ for the relevant category of modules, let $H^i_-$ denote minus Drinfeld–Sokolov reduction, and let $L(\ta{ lambda})$ and ${\bf L}(\gamma_{\bar{\ta{ lambda}}})$ denote the corresponding simple modules. A weight $\ta{ lambda}$ is non-critical when it does not lie on the critical hyperplane.

**Minus-reduction conjecture.** For any $\ta{ kappa}\in\mathbb C$ and any $V\in\operatorname{Obj}\ta{ O}_{\ta{ kappa}$},

$$
H^i_-(V)=0\qquad (i\ne 0).
$$

For any non-critical weight $\ta{ lambda}$,

$$
H^0_-(L(\ta{ lambda}))\cong
\begin{cases}
{\bf L}(\gamma_{\bar{\ta{ lambda}}})&\text{if }\langle \ta{ lambda}+\rho,\bar{\ta{ alpha}}^{\vee}\rangle\notin\{1,2,\dots\}\text{ for all }\bar{\ta{ alpha}}\in\bar{\ta{ Delta}}_+,\\
0&\text{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
$$

This predicts exactness of minus Drinfeld–Sokolov reduction on the specified category and identifies its effect on simple modules. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence, so the conjecture is recorded as open.

D32.title: Fricke-sign conjecture for theta congruences in weights 2 and 4
D32.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $S_k(\overline{\mathbf{Z}}_p)$ denote the new cusp forms of weight $k$ and level $\Gamma_0(p)$ over the algebraic integers, let $w_p$ be the Fricke involution, and let $\theta$ be the operator on $q$-expansions given by $\theta(\sum a_nq^n)=\sum n a_nq^n$.

**Fricke-sign conjecture.** If $f\in S_2(\overline{\mathbf{Z}}_p)$ and $g\in S_4(\overline{\mathbf{Z}}_p)$ are eigenforms satisfying $\theta f\equiv g\pmod p$, then the $w_p$-eigenvalues of $f$ and $g$ have opposite signs.

This predicts that theta-induced congruences in these weights occur across the two Fricke eigenspaces, and is used in the paper to formulate an exact sequence relating the corresponding mod-$p$ spaces. Its resolution status is not specified in the source.

D32.title: AMU conjecture on detecting pseudo-Anosov mapping classes by TQFT representations
D32.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be the surface with mapping class group $\Gamma$, and let $\rho_k$ denote the level-$k$ TQFT representation of $\Gamma$. A mapping class is **Pseudo-Anosov** if it is pseudo-Anosov, and it is reducible with pseudo-Anosov pieces if its canonical reduction has pseudo-Anosov components.

**AMU conjecture.** For a mapping class $\phi\in\Gamma$, $\phi$ is Pseudo-Anosov or reducible with Pseudo-Anosov pieces if and only if $\rho_k(\phi)$ is infinite order for large enough $k$.

This conjecture proposes that the asymptotic order of TQFT representations detects precisely the mapping classes having pseudo-Anosov dynamics on at least one component. The supplied text presents it as an expectation, and gives no resolution.

D32.title: Mazur's principle for U(2,1) Shimura varieties
D32.statement:
Let $U$ be a level subgroup with local component $U_{\mathfrak p}=\Gamma_{i_0,\dots,i_r}$, and let $m$ be a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra associated with $U$. Call $m$ **pseudo-Eisenstein** if either

$$
H^{n-1}_{\text{\rm \tiny 'et}}((X_U)_{\overline{F}_{\mathfrak p}},{\mathbb Z}_l)^{\text{\rm \tiny tor}}_m\ne 0,
$$

or $H^i_{\text{\rm \tiny 'et}}((X_U)_{\overline{F}_{\mathfrak p}},{\mathbb Z}_l)_m\ne 0$ for some $i\ne n-1$. Let $\overline{\rho}_m$ be the mod $m$ Galois representation, let $l$ be the residue characteristic of $m$ with $l\ne p$, and let $N$ be the monodromy operator on a representation space for $\overline{\rho}_m$.

**Mazur's principle.** Suppose that $m$ is not pseudo-Eisenstein and that $N^r=0$ on a representation space for $\overline{\rho}_m$. Then there is a level $U'$ containing $U$, isomorphic to $U$ away from $\mathfrak p$, with

$$
U'_{\mathfrak p}=\Gamma_{i'_0,\dots,i'_{r'}},\qquad r'<r,
$$

such that $\overline{\rho}_m$ arises from level $U'$.

This is a converse to the necessary monodromy-vanishing condition for lowering the level at $\mathfrak p$, extending the role of Mazur's principle from modular curves to these unitary Shimura varieties. The supplied text does not establish the conjecture or state results proving it, so its resolution status is left open.

D32.title: The WLP characterization conjecture for level Artinian almost complete intersections
D32.statement:
Let $R=K[x,y,z]$, and let

$$
I=(x^{\alpha+t},y^{\beta+t},z^{\gamma+t},x^\alpha y^\beta z^\gamma)
$$

be a level Artinian almost complete intersection, where $t>0$ and $0\leq\alpha\leq\beta\leq\gamma$. Assume that $K$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero. The **WLP characterization conjecture.** The quotient $R/I$ has the WLP whenever at least one of the following holds: (a) $\alpha=0$; (b) $\alpha+\beta+\gamma$ is not divisible by $3$; (c) $\gamma>2(\alpha+\beta)$; or (d) $t<\frac{1}{3}(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)$. If $1\leq\alpha\leq\beta\leq\gamma\leq2(\alpha+\beta)$, $\alpha+\beta+\gamma\equiv0\pmod 3$, and $t\geq\frac{1}{3}(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)$, then $R/I$ fails to have the WLP if and only if $t$ is even and either (i) $\alpha$ is even, $\alpha=\beta$, and $\gamma-\alpha\equiv3\pmod 6$, or (ii) $\alpha$ is odd and either $\alpha=\beta$ with $\gamma-\alpha\equiv0\pmod 6$, or $\beta=\gamma$ with $\gamma-\alpha\equiv0\pmod 3$. In all these cases, the Hilbert function has twin peaks. The claim gives a proposed complete characterization of the weak Lefschetz property in this family, extending the preceding semistability and congruence criteria; its status is not resolved in the supplied source context.

D32.title: Benedetti–Guadagnini conjecture on CMC marked spectra
D32.statement:
Let $M$ be a future complete $MGHC$ non-elementary flat space-time of dimension $2+1$, and let $T_{cmc}$ be its associated $CMC$ time. For each $a>0$, let $(S^{T_{cmc}}_a,d^{T_{cmc}}_a)$ be the metric space associated with the level set of $T_{cmc}$ at time $a$, and for $\gamma\in\pi_1(M)$ define its marked length by

$$
l_a^{T_{cmc}}(\gamma)=\inf_{x\in S^{T_{cmc}}_a}d^{T_{cmc}}_a(x,\gamma.x).
$$

**Benedetti–Guadagnini conjecture.** For every $\gamma\in\pi_1(M)$,

$$
\lim_{a\rightarrow 0}l_a^{T_{cmc}}(\gamma)=l_{\Sigma}(\gamma),
$$

and

$$
\lim_{a\rightarrow +\infty}a^{-1}l_a^{T_{cmc}}(\gamma)=l_{\mathbb{H}^2}(\gamma).
$$

The conjecture predicts that the CMC level-set marked spectra converge at the initial singularity to the spectrum $l_{\Sigma}$ and, after rescaling, at late times to the hyperbolic spectrum $l_{\mathbb{H}^2}$. The supplied text gives no resolution status.

D32.title: The modularity conjecture for elliptic curves and QM surfaces over imaginary quadratic fields
D32.statement:
Let $K$ be an imaginary quadratic field. A **Bianchi newform** over $K$ is a weight-$2$ cuspidal eigenform of level $[?]$ with rational Hecke eigenvalues; here $[?]$ denotes the ideal level, and a **QM surface** is an abelian surface with quaternion multiplication. **Modularity conjecture.**

1. If $f$ is a Bianchi newform over $K$ of weight $2$ and level $\Gamma_0(\mathfrak{n})$ with rational Hecke eigenvalues, then either there is an elliptic curve $E/K$ without CM by $K$ of conductor $\mathfrak{n}$ such that

$$
L(E/K,s)=L(f,s),
$$

or there is a QM surface $A/K$ of conductor $\mathfrak{n}^2$ such that

$$
L(A/K,s)=L(f,s)^2.
$$

2. Conversely, if $E/K$ is an elliptic curve without CM by $K$ of conductor $\mathfrak{n}$, then there is an $f$ as above such that

$$
L(E,s)=L(f,s).
$$

Moreover, if $A/K$ is a QM surface of conductor $\mathfrak{n}^2$, then there is an $f$ as above such that

$$
L(A,s)=L(f,s)^2.
$$

This conjecture extends the correspondence between elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ and classical weight-$2$ newforms to imaginary quadratic fields, where quaternion-multiplication surfaces must also be included. The paper gives explicit examples of genuine QM abelian surfaces that are modular, but the general correspondence asserted here remains unresolved.

D32.title: The edge-map conjecture for integral modular forms on $\mathcal{M}_0(n)$
D32.statement:
For every positive integer $n$, let $\operatorname{TMF}_0(n)$ denote the associated spectrum of topological modular forms and let $\operatorname{MF}_0(n)_0$ denote the degree-zero modular forms for the moduli problem with level-$\Gamma_0(n)$ structure. The natural edge map

$$
\pi_0\operatorname{TMF}_0(n)\to \operatorname{MF}_0(n)_0
$$

is defined by the descent spectral sequence. **Edge-map conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$, this natural edge map is an isomorphism. Such an isomorphism would allow the relevant argument to proceed without inverting $\gcd(6,\phi(n))$; the source introduces it as a conjectural way to remove that localisation hypothesis, and gives no resolution.

D32.title: Böcherer–Kikuta's generalization conjecture for mod $p^m$ singular forms
D32.statement: Let $n$, $k$, and $N$ be positive integers, let $r$ be an even integer, and let $p$ be a prime. Let $\chi$ be a quadratic Dirichlet character modulo $N$ satisfying $\chi(-1)=(-1)^k$. Suppose that $F\in M_k(\Gamma_0^{(n+r)}(N),\chi)_{\mathbb Z_{(p)}}$ is mod $p^m$ singular of $p$-rank $r$. The proven theorem assumes $n\ge r$ and $p>r+1$, and expresses $F$ modulo $p^m$ as a finite linear combination of theta series satisfying the stated modularity and level-divisibility conditions. **Böcherer–Kikuta's generalization conjecture.** Theorem general should hold for any prime, not only for $p>r+1$, and without the assumption $n\ge r$. This would extend the structure theorem to small primes and to the range $n<r$, where the theorem in the paper does not apply.

D32.title: $GL(3)$ Kuznetsov trace formula in the level aspect
D32.statement:
Develop a Kuznetsov trace formula for automorphic forms for the group $\Gamma_0(N) = \left\lbrace \begin{pmatrix} \star & \star & \star \\ \star & \star & \star \\ 0 & 0 & \star \end{pmatrix} \bmod N \right\rbrace$ for any integer $N\geq1$.

For the purpose of applications, develop a Kuznetsov trace formula for automorphic forms for the group $\Gamma_B(N) = \left\lbrace \begin{pmatrix} \star & \star & \star \\ 0 & \star & \star \\ 0 & 0 & \star \end{pmatrix} \bmod N \right\rbrace$.

D32.title: Asymptotic for second moment of $\rm GL_2\times GL_2$ in level aspect
D32.statement:
Let $\mathcal{B}_k(p)$ be a basis for holomorphic or Hecke-Maass forms for $\Gamma_0(p)\subset SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ of weight $k$. Obtain an asymptotic with a power saving error term for the second moment

$$
\sum_{f\in\mathcal{B}_k(p)}\sum_{g\in\mathcal{B}_\ell(q)} |L(1/2, f\times g)|^2,
$$

as the level $p$ and $q$ become larger, the weights $k$ and $\ell$ are fixed.

D32.title: Subconvexity bound for $\rm GL_3\times GL_2$ in level aspect
D32.statement: Let $\pi$ be a fixed Hecke-Maass cusp form for $SL_3(\mathbb{Z})$ and $f$ be a holomorphic for Hecke Maass cusp form for $\Gamma_0(M)$. Obtain a subconvexity bound estimate for $L(1/2, \pi\times f)$ as $M$ grows.

D32.title: Shifted convolution sum for $\rm GL_3\times GL_2$ in level aspect
D32.statement:
Let $\pi$ be a fixed Hecke-Maass cusp form for $SL_3(\mathbb{Z})$ with Fourier coefficients $\{\lambda_\pi(r,n)\}$ and $f$ be a holomorphic for Hecke Maass cusp form for $\Gamma_0(M)$ with Fourier coefficients $\{\lambda_f(n)\}$. Obtain a non-trivial bound for the shifted sum,

$$
\sum_{n<N}\lambda_\pi(r,n)\lambda_f(n+1),
$$

in the convexity range $N\sim M^{3/2}$.

D32.title: Geometric local systems on $\mathcal{M}_g$ and rigidity
D32.statement:
Consider a local system $\mathbb{L}$ on $\mathcal{M}_g$ (or a space with some level structure) or equivalently a representation of $\mathrm{Mod}(\Sigma_g)$ (or correspondingly a representation of some finite index subgroup). Suppose $\mathbb{L}$ underlies a variation of Hodge structures. Is the period map $\mathcal{M}_g \to D / \Gamma$ rigid in some sense? We can ask: is ther period map

(1) isolated in its mapping space

(2) infinitesimally rigid

(3) is it actually unique as a nonconstant map.

D32.title: Relative Homology
D32.statement:
Given graphs $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma'$, where $\Gamma$ is obtained from $\Gamma'$ via an edge deletion, can we compute $H_i(\overline{\operatorname{Conf}}_n(\Gamma'),\overline{\operatorname{Conf}}_n(\Gamma))$. 

If $\Gamma$ is obtained from $\Gamma'$ via an edge contraction, we have an induced map on the level of chain complexes. Can we compute the homology of the mapping cone of this map on chain complexes?

D32.title: Multivariate analysis
D32.statement: Random matrix theory was introduced into theoretical physics by Wigner in the 1950s in his study of neutron scattering resonances, but as a subject, RMT goes back to the work of statisticians at the beginning of the 20th century. Recently, advances in RMT have opened the way to the statistical analysis of data sets in cases where the number of variables is comparable to the number of samples, and both are large. One might, for example, be interested in the daily temperature in hundreds of cities around the world, over a 365 day time period. At the technical level, one considers the statistics of the singular values of (appropriately centered and scaled) $p\times n$ matrices $M=(M_{ij})$, where $p\sim n\to\infty$. Here $p$ is the number of variables and $n$ is the sample size. More precisely, one centers the $M_{ij}$'s around their sample averages, $$ M_{ij}\to\hat M_{ij}=M_{ij}-\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n M_{ik}, $$ and considers the eigenvalues $l_1\geq\cdots\geq l_p\geq0$ and associated eigenvectors $w_1,\dots,w_p$ of the $p\times p$ sample matrix $S=\frac1n \hat M \hat M^T$. The $l_i$'s and $w_i$'s are known as the principal component eigenvalues and eigenvectors, respectively. In Principal Component Analysis (PCA) ``significant'' dimension reduction in the data occurs if the first few principal components $l_1, l_2,...$ account for a ``high'' proportion of the total variance $\operatorname{tr} S=\sum_{j=1}^p l_j$. A common model for the variables $M_{ij}$ is to assume that they follow a (real) $p$-variate Gaussian distribution $N_p(\mu,\Sigma)$ with mean $\mu$ and covariance matrix $\Sigma$. Thus the columns $(M_{1j}, M_{2j},\dots, M_{pj})^T$ provide $n$ independent samples for $N_p(\mu,\Sigma)$. Using recent results from RMT, much has now been proved about the statistics of $l_1, l_2,...$ as $p,n\to\infty$, $p/n\to\gamma\in(0,\infty)$, in the case $\Sigma=I$. In particular, we know that in the limit, $l_1$, appropriately centered and scaled, satisfies the Tracy-Widom distribution for the largest eigenvalues of a GOE matrix. However, most interesting applications involve so-called spiked populations, a terminology introduced by Johnstone, i.e. situations where most of the eigenvalues $\eta_1,...,\eta_p$ of $\Sigma$ are equal to a common value, say 1, but the first few eigenvalues are greater than 1. Thus $$ \eta_1\geq\eta_2\geq\cdots\geq\eta_k>\eta_{k+1}=\cdots=\eta_p=1 $$ for some fixed $k<<p$. It is a major problem in multivariate analysis to analyze the statistics of the eigenvalues $l_1, l_2,...$ as $p,n\to\infty$, $p/n\to\gamma\in(0,\infty)$ for such spiked populations. There are very interesting phase transitions in the theory. For example if $\eta_1>1+\sqrt{\gamma}$, then, as $p\sim n\to\infty$, $l_1$ emerges from the Marchenko-Pastur continuum $\bigl((\sqrt\gamma-1)^2,(\sqrt\gamma+1)^2\bigr)$, where most of the $l_j$'s tend to accumulate, and almost surely $$ l_1\to\eta_1 \cdot \Bigl(1+\frac{\gamma}{\eta_1-1}\Bigr)>(1+\sqrt\gamma)^2\,. $$ In the spiked, complex case, i.e. when the columns $(M_{1j},M_{2j},...,M_{pj})^T$ are sampled from the complex $p$-variate Gaussian distribution, much is known about the asymptotic distribution of the $l_j$'s, as $p,n\to\infty$, $p/n\to\gamma\in(0,\infty)$. By contrast in the real case, apart from a.s. convergence of the $l_i$'s, very little is known about their asymptotic distributions. In the spiked, complex case the analysis is enabled by a particular technical tool, the Harish-Chandra-Itzykson-Zuber formula: unfortunately, no analog of this formula is known in the real case. While there are relatively few applications of complex spiked populations, knowledge of the asymptotic distributions of the $l_i$'s for real spiked populations would have immediate applications to a wide variety of problems in signal processing, genetics and finance.

D32.title: Modularity of the arithmetic generating series from special divisors on a Shimura curve
D32.statement: Theorem 1.2. The Laurent series \(\widehat{\phi}_1=\sum_t\widehat{Z}_t(v)q^t\), with \(\widehat{Z}_0(v)=-[\widehat{\omega}]-(0,\log v+c)\), is a non-holomorphic modular form of weight \(3/2\) and level \(\Gamma_0(4D(B))\), with values in \(\widehat{\mathrm{CH}}^1(M)\). Here \(D(B)\) is the product of the ramification primes of \(B\).

D32.title: Selberg eigenvalue conjecture for principal congruence subgroups
D32.statement:
Let \(\Gamma(N)\subset SL(2,\mathbb Z)\) be the principal congruence subgroup of level \(N\), and let \(X(N)=\Gamma(N)\backslash\mathbb H\). The Selberg conjecture asks whether the first positive eigenvalue \(\lambda_1(X(N))\) of the Laplacian satisfies

$$\lambda_1(X(N))\ge \frac14$$

for all \(N\).

D32.title: Yoshida-type liftings to level-2 Siegel modular forms
D32.statement:
For the regular pair $(l,m)$ considered in the report, let $\Gamma_2[2]=\ker\bigl(\operatorname{Sp}(4,\mathbb Z)\to\operatorname{Sp}(4,\mathbb Z/2)\bigr)$. If $f\in S_{l+m+4}(\Gamma_0(2))^{\mathrm{new}}$ and $g\in S_{l-m+2}(\Gamma_0(2))^{\mathrm{new}}$ are newforms, then there exists a Siegel modular form $F\in S_{l-m,m+3}(\Gamma_2[2])$ that is an eigenform for the Hecke algebra and satisfies
\[
L(F,s)=L(f,s)L(g,s-m-1).
\]
It occurs with multiplicity $5$ if $f$ and $g$ have the same eigenvalue $\pm$ under the Atkin–Lehner involution $w_2$, and with multiplicity $1$ otherwise. Similarly, for newforms $f\in S_{l+m+4}(\Gamma_0(4))^{\mathrm{new}}$ and $g\in S_{l-m+2}(\Gamma_0(4))^{\mathrm{new}}$, there exists a Siegel modular form $F\in S_{l-m,m+3}(\Gamma_2[2])$ with spinor $L$-function
\[
L(F,s)=L(f,s)L(g,s-m-1),
\]
and it occurs with multiplicity $5$ in $S_{l-m,m+3}(\Gamma_2[2])$.

D32.title: Yoshida-type lifting at level 2
D32.statement:
Let $f\in S_{l+m+4}(\Gamma_0(2))^{\mathrm{new}}$ and $g\in S_{l-m+2}(\Gamma_0(2))^{\mathrm{new}}$ be newforms. Then there exists a Siegel modular form $F\in S_{l-m,m+3}(\Gamma_2[2])$ that is an eigenform for the Hecke algebra and has spinor $L$-function
\[
L(F,s)=L(f,s)L(g,s-m-1).
\]
Moreover, $F$ occurs with multiplicity $5$ if $f$ and $g$ have the same eigenvalue $\pm1$ under $w_2$, and with multiplicity $1$ otherwise.

D32.title: Counterexamples to the De Giorgi conjecture in dimensions $N\ge 9$
D32.statement:
For every $N\ge 9$ and every sufficiently small $\alpha>0$, there exists a bounded solution $u_\alpha:\mathbb{R}^N\to\mathbb{R}$ of
$$
\Delta u+(1-u^2)u=0
$$
such that $u_\alpha(0)=0$, $\partial_{x_N}u_\alpha(x)>0$ for all $x\in\mathbb{R}^N$, and $|u_\alpha(x)|\to1$ as $\operatorname{dist}(x,\Gamma_\alpha)\to+\infty$, uniformly for small $\alpha>0$, where $\Gamma_\alpha=\alpha^{-1}\Gamma$ and $\Gamma=\{x_9=F(x')\}$ is the dilated Bombieri–De Giorgi–Giusti minimal graph. These solutions provide nonplanar monotone level sets and hence counterexamples in dimensions $N\ge9$.

D32.title: Maximum number of zeros of Abelian integrals
D32.statement:
For fixed integers $m,n$, determine $Z(m,n)$, the maximum number of isolated zeros, counted with multiplicities, of the Abelian integrals
\[
I(h)=\oint_{\gamma_h}\bigl(f(x,y)\,dy-g(x,y)\,dx\bigr),
\]
where $H,f,g$ are real polynomials of degrees $m,n,n$, respectively, and $\{\gamma_h\}_{h\in(a,b)}$ is a family of ovals contained in the level curves $H=h$ and filling an annulus. The integral is assumed not to vanish identically on $(a,b)$, and the zeros are taken for $h\in(a,b)$.

D32.title: Fuchs–Schweigert formula for the unmarked moduli space
D32.statement:
Let $G'=G/Z$, where $Z=Z(G)$, and let $
\Sigma$ be a closed surface of genus $g$. For a level $k$ satisfying $P^\vee\!\cdot P^\vee\subset k^{-1}\mathbb Z$, and a choice of pre-quantization with phase factor $\varphi:Z^{2g}\to U(1)$, the quantization of the trivial-bundle component $M_{G'}(\Sigma)=D(G')^g\!//G$ is
\[
Q\bigl(M_{G'}(\Sigma)\bigr)=\frac{1}{|Z|^{2g}}\sum_{\gamma=(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_{2g})\in Z^{2g}}\varphi(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_{2g})\sum_{\lambda\in P_k^\gamma}S_{0,\lambda}^{\,2-2g},
\]
where $P_k^\gamma$ is the set of level-$k$ weights fixed by the action of every component of $\gamma$ and $S$ is the Verlinde $S$-matrix. The report presents this as the formula conjectured by Fuchs and Schweigert and derives it.

D32.title: Mazur–Gouvêa conjecture on $p$-adic analytic families of modular eigenforms
D32.statement: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $N$ relatively prime to $p$, a Dirichlet character $\chi:(\mathbb Z/(pN))^*\to\mathbb C^*$, and let $S_k^\alpha$ denote the slope-$\alpha$ subspace of cusp forms of weight $k$, level $\Gamma_1(pN)$, and nebentype $\chi\omega^{-k}$. The Mazur–Gouvêa conjecture stated in the report asserts that every eigenform $f_0\in S_{k_0}^\alpha$ fits into a $p$-adic analytic family of eigenforms of varying weight: there exist a finite flat $\mathbb Z_p[[X]]$-algebra $R$, morphisms $\eta_k:R\to\overline{\mathbb Q}_p$, and a formal $q$-expansion $F=\sum_{n>0}A_nq^n\in R[[q]]$ such that, for every $k$, the specialization $f_k=\eta_k(F)=\sum_{n>0}\eta_k(A_n)q^n$ is an eigenform in $S_k^\alpha$, and $f_{k_0}=f_0$.

D32.title: Long periods for quantised Anosov toral automorphisms for almost all levels
D32.statement:
Let \(\kappa\in\Gamma_\theta=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\in\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z):ab\equiv dc\equiv0\pmod 2\right\}\) be an Anosov map, and define
\[
\operatorname{ord}(\kappa,N)=\min\{p\in\mathbb N:\kappa^p\equiv I\pmod N\}.
\]
Then, for a subset of \(N\in\mathbb N\) of natural density one, there exists a constant \(\delta>0\) such that
\[
\operatorname{ord}(\kappa,N)\gg N^{1/2}\exp\bigl((\log N)^\delta\bigr).
\]

D32.title: AGT conjecture for the one-vertex, one-loop quiver variety
D32.statement: Let \(\Gamma\) be the quiver with one vertex and one loop, let \(r\ge 0\), and let \(M_r\) be the corresponding quiver variety, namely the moduli space of torsion-free sheaves of rank \(r\) on \(\mathbb P^2\) with a trivialisation over a fixed line \(\mathbb P^1\subset\mathbb P^2\). Let \(D=(\mathbb C^\times)^{r+2}\) act through the \((\mathbb C^\times)^2\)-action on \(\mathbb P^2\) and the \((\mathbb C^\times)^r\)-action on the trivialisation. With \(R_r=H_D(\mathrm{point})=\mathbb C[x,y,e_1,\ldots,e_r]\), \(\vec e=(e_1,\ldots,e_r)\), \(\kappa=-y/x\), and \(L^K_r=H_D(M_r)\otimes_{R_r}K_r\), where \(K_r\) is the fraction field of \(R_r\), the following hold: (a) \(L^K_r\) admits a representation of the affine \(W\)-algebra \(W_k(\mathfrak{gl}_r)\) at level \(k=\kappa-r\), identifying it with the Verma module of highest weight \(\beta=\vec e/y-\xi\rho/\kappa\); (b) this action is quasi-unitary with respect to the intersection pairing on \(L^K_r\); and (c) the Gaiotto state \(G=\sum_{n\ge 0}G_n\), with \(G_n=[M_{r,n}]\), is a Whittaker vector of this Verma module.

D32.title: Adem–Ge–Pan–Petrosyan conjecture on the Lyndon–Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence
D32.statement: Conjecture 2 (Adem–Ge–Pan–Petrosyan): The Lyndon–Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence associated to the semidirect product $\Gamma := \mathbb{Z}^n \rtimes_{\rho} \mathbb{Z}/m$ collapses in the strongest sense: all differentials in the $E_r$-term for $r \ge 2$ are trivial and all extension problems at the $E_\infty$-level are trivial. In particular, for all $k \ge 0$, $H^k(\Gamma;\mathbb{Z}) \cong \bigoplus_{i+j=k} H^i(\mathbb{Z}/m;H^j(\mathbb{Z}^n))$.

D32.title: Higher-order finite element methods for surface PDEs from an approximate level-set function
D32.statement:
Can one develop a higher-order finite element method for the Laplace–Beltrami equation on a stationary smooth surface $\Gamma$ when $\Gamma$ is the zero level of a smooth level-set function $\phi$, but only a finite-element approximation $\phi_h^k$ of $\phi$ is available? Assume that $\phi_h^k$ belongs to a standard finite-element space on a quasi-uniform triangulation of a bulk domain containing $\Gamma$ and satisfies
\[
\|\phi_h^k-\phi\|_{L^\infty(U)}+h\|\phi_h^k-\phi\|_{H^1_\infty(U)}\le c h^{k+1},
\]
where $U$ is a small neighborhood of $\Gamma$ in $\mathbb R^3$.

D32.title: Many-body localization for a disordered interacting quantum spin chain
D32.statement:
For the random-field, random-transverse-field, random-exchange Ising Hamiltonian
\[
H=\sum_{i=-K}^{K}h_iS_i^z+\sum_{i=-K}^{K}\gamma_iS_i^x+\sum_{i=-K}^{K-1}J_iS_i^zS_{i+1}^z
\]
on \(\Lambda=[-K,K]\cap\mathbb Z\), acting on \(\mathcal H=\bigotimes_{i\in\Lambda}\mathbb C^2\), where \(S_i^z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}\), \(S_i^x=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\), \(\gamma_i=\gamma\Gamma_i\), and \(h_i,\Gamma_i,J_i\) are independent, bounded random variables with bounded probability densities: does localization persist for the interacting system, in the sense that one can establish full many-body localization (complete diagonalization by quasilocal transformations, equivalently a complete set of local integrals of motion) without assuming the level-statistics hypothesis LLA? The report formulates LLA as
\[
\mathbb P\!\left(\min_{\alpha\ne\beta}|E_\alpha-E_\beta|<\delta\right)\le \delta^{\nu Cn}\qquad(\delta>0),
\]
for the Hamiltonian in boxes of size \(n\).

D32.title: Limited level-attraction bound for a random interacting spin chain
D32.statement:
For the random-field, random-transverse-field, random-exchange Ising Hamiltonian on \(\Lambda=[-K,K]\cap\mathbb Z\),
\[
H=\sum_{i=-K}^{K}h_iS_i^z+\sum_{i=-K}^{K}\gamma_iS_i^x+\sum_{i=-K}^{K-1}J_iS_i^zS_{i+1}^z,
\]
acting on \(\mathcal H=\bigotimes_{i\in\Lambda}\mathbb C^2\), where \(S_i^z\) and \(S_i^x\) are the Pauli matrices acting at site \(i\), \(\gamma_i=\gamma\Gamma_i\) with \(\gamma\) sufficiently small, and \(h_i,\Gamma_i,J_i\) are independent bounded random variables with bounded probability densities, establish the limited-level-attraction estimate: for some \(\nu>0\) and \(C<\infty\), for every \(\delta>0\) and every box size \(n\),
\[
\mathbb P\!\left(\min_{\alpha\ne\beta}|E_\alpha-E_\beta|<\delta\right)\le \delta^{\nu}C n,
\]
where \(E_\alpha\) are the eigenvalues of the Hamiltonian in the box.

D32.title: Finite-family analogue for a two-element Rogers semilattice
D32.statement: For a level $n\ge 2$, does there exist a finite family $S$ of $\Sigma^{-1}_n$ sets whose Rogers semilattice $R^{-1}_n(S)$ of $\Sigma^{-1}_n$-computable numberings has exactly two distinct elements $\alpha$ and $\beta$, where $\alpha$ is a Friedberg $\Sigma^{-1}_n$-computable numbering and, for every $\Sigma^{-1}_n$-computable numbering $\gamma$ of $S$, if $\alpha$ is not equivalent to $\gamma$, then $\beta\leq\gamma$?

D32.title: Quantum ergodicity for compact quotients of $\mathrm{SL}_d(\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SO}(d)$ in the level aspect
D32.statement:
Let $d\ge 3$, $S=\mathrm{SL}_d(\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SO}(d)$, and let $\Gamma_n\le \mathrm{SL}_d(\mathbb{R})$ be a sequence of uniformly discrete, torsion-free, cocompact lattices such that $\operatorname{vol}(\Gamma_n ackslash S)	o\infty$. u_{n,j}\in\mathfrak a^*_\mathbb C/W$. Then there exists $\varrho>0$ such that, for every sufficiently regular $
