D32.title: Hambly–Lyons isometry conjecture for reduced bounded-variation paths
D32.statement:
For every reduced bounded-variation path \(\gamma:[0,T]\to\mathbb{R}^d\), the conjectured isometry is
\[
\|\gamma\|_{1\text{-var}}=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\bigl\|n!X^n_{0,T}\bigr\|^{1/n},
\]
where \(X^n_{0,T}\) is the \(n\)-th level of the signature \(S(\gamma)_{0,T}\), and \(\|\cdot\|\) is the projective norm (on the relevant tensor powers induced by the norm on \(\mathbb{R}^d\)).

D32.title: Other branching reference processes for unbalanced optimal transport
D32.statement:
When the reference law \(R\) is the law of a branching Brownian motion with \(p_0=p_2=1/2\), and \(
u	o0\) with \(\lambda\sim 
u^{-1}e^{-1/
u}\), the \(\Gamma\)-convergence at the PDE level towards optimal partial transport can be shown, corresponding to \(\Psi(r)=|r|\). Is it possible to obtain other unbalanced optimal transport models—especially the model with \(\Psi(r)=r^2\)—by using other kinds of branching processes as a reference law?

D33.title: Dyadic denominator law for the phase constants of the Jacobi zeros
D33.statement:
Let $\kappa_r(A,B)\in\mathbb{Q}[A,B]$ be the $r$-th additive phase constant in the asymptotic phase equation for the zeros of Jacobi polynomials, with $A=\alpha^2$ and $B= eta^2$. If $\operatorname{den}(\kappa_r)$ denotes the least positive integer clearing the denominators of all coefficients of $\kappa_r$, prove that, for every integer $r\geq 1$, $
u_2(\operatorname{den}(\kappa_r))=E_r$, where $E_r=3r-1+
u_2((r-1)!)$. Equivalently, $2^{E_r}\kappa_r\in\mathbb{Z}_2[A,B]$, while $2^{E_r-1}\kappa_r
otin\mathbb{Z}_2[A,B]$. The established odd-part bound is that the odd part of $\operatorname{den}(\kappa_r)$ divides $\operatorname{lcm}(1,3,\ldots,2r-1)$; the sharp conjecture concerns the exact dyadic exponent.

D34.title: Cascade-channel capacity conjecture for finite-state channels
D34.statement:
Let $p(y(i),s(i+1)\mid x(i),s(i))$ be a state-dependent channel with finite input and output alphabets satisfying $|\mathcal X|=|\mathcal Y|<\infty$. For a channel with memory, let $C_0$ denote its zero-error capacity, let $C_0^m$ denote the zero-error capacity of the $m$-fold cascade channel, and define

$$
C_0^{\inf}=\lim_{m\to\infty}C_0^m.
$$

**Cascade-channel capacity conjecture.** If $|\mathcal S|<\infty$, so that the channel is finite-state, then the Shannon capacity of the $m$-fold cascade channel converges to $C_0^{\inf}$ as $m\to\infty$. Conversely, there exist channels with finite input and output alphabets and infinite state space $|\mathcal S|=\infty$ for which the Shannon capacity of the cascade channel converges, as $m\to\infty$, to a value strictly larger than $C_0^{\inf}$.

The conjecture distinguishes finite-state channels, where asymptotic cascade capacity is predicted to equal the limiting zero-error capacity, from channels with infinite memory, where a strict separation can occur. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

D34.title: Convergence of cascade tree decomposition KL divergence to zero
D34.statement: Let $\underline{X}$ be the input random vector and let $\underline{X}_{{\mathcal M}_i}$ denote the model random vector obtained after $i$ cascade-tree stages. Write ${\mathcal D}(f_{\underline{X}}(\underline{x})\,||\,f_{\underline{X}_{{\mathcal M}_i}}(\underline{x}))$ for the Kullback–Leibler divergence between their distributions. **Convergence conjecture.** The KL divergence converges to $0$ as the number of cascade trees $i$ increases. The preceding theorem establishes only that this divergence decreases and converges to a finite value; whether the limiting value is $0$ is the conjectured strengthening.

D34.title: Right-eigenvalue conjecture for the context-tree matrix
D34.statement:
Let a **probabilised context tree** be given, with associated square matrix $Q$, and let ${\mathscr S}$ denote the set of alpha-LIS objects. For each $\alpha s\in{\mathscr S}$, let $\left(\kappa_{\alpha s}(n)\right)_n$ be the associated sequence.

**Right-eigenvalue conjecture.** If, for every $\alpha s\in{\mathscr S}$, the sequence $\left(\kappa_{\alpha s}(n)\right)_n$ converges to $0$, then $Q$ admits $1$ as a right eigenvalue.

When the context tree is stable, the matrix $Q$ is stochastic under the same vanishing condition. The conjecture asks whether the right eigenvalue still exists without stability; together with the stated correspondence between right eigenvectors and invariant measures, it would imply existence of an invariant probability measure when the set of alpha-LIS is finite and all cascade series converge.

D34.title: Geometric convergence conjecture for cascade series
D34.statement:
Let a **non-null probabilised context tree** be given, and consider its cascade series. A subtree is **shift-stable** when it is preserved by the relevant shift operation.

**Geometric convergence conjecture.** If the tree has no infinite shift-stable subtree, then all its cascade series converge with geometric rates.

The conjecture is motivated by the contrast between the left comb, whose cascade series may converge or diverge depending on the distributions, and the bamboo blossom, whose cascade series converge geometrically for every non-null choice of distributions. The claim remains an open proposed generalization of these examples.

D34.title: Vanishing-of-cascades conjecture for sigma-finite invariant measures
D34.statement:
Let $U$ be a variable-length memory chain defined by a **probabilised stable context tree**, and suppose that $U$ admits an invariant $\sigma$-finite measure. For every $\alpha s\in{\mathscr S}$, let $\left(\kappa_{\alpha s}(n)\right)_n$ be the associated sequence, where ${\mathscr S}$ is the set of alpha-LIS objects.

**Vanishing-of-cascades conjecture.** For every $\alpha s\in{\mathscr S}$, the sequence $\left(\kappa_{\alpha s}(n)\right)_n$ tends to $0$ as $n$ tends to infinity. Consequently, $Q$ is stochastic.

For stable context trees, vanishing of cascades already implies that $Q$ is stochastic, while convergence of cascade series is known to be necessary for an invariant probability measure. The conjecture proposes the analogous necessity of vanishing cascades for the existence of an invariant $\sigma$-finite measure.

D36.title: Sign conjecture for Steiner distance hyperdeterminants
D36.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree on $n$ vertices, let $M$ be its order-$k$ Steiner distance hypermatrix, and write $\operatorname{sgn}(x)$ for $1$ if $x>0$, $-1$ if $x<0$, and $0$ if $x=0$.

**Sign conjecture.** For any tree on $n$ vertices,

$$
\operatorname{sgn}(\det(M))=(-1)^{n-1}
$$

when this quantity is nonzero.

The conjecture appears in earlier work and has been checked numerically for $(k,n)=(4,4)$, $(4,5)$, and $(6,4)$. It is trivially true for $n\leq 3$ and odd $k$, and follows from Graham–Pollak when $k=2$; its general status is not established in the supplied text.

D38.title: The edge-irregularity deletion conjecture
D38.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be a connected graph, and let $m=|E|$ be its number of edges. An **edge-irregulator** of $G$ is a set $S\subseteq E$ such that $G-S$ is locally irregular, meaning that every edge of $G-S$ joins vertices of different degrees; write ${\rm I}_e(G)$ for the minimum possible size of an edge-irregulator. **Edge-irregularity deletion conjecture.** There is an absolute constant $c\geq 1$ such that, for every connected graph $G$ with $m$ edges,

$$
{\rm I}_e(G)\leq \frac{1}{3}m+c.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the behaviour of cycles, where deleting one edge can resolve at most three local degree conflicts, while small graphs such as $K_2$ and $C_4$ show that an additive constant is necessary. The general bound remains open in the source paper.

D39.title: Folklore conjecture on the reverse entropy power inequality for i.i.d. log-concave random vectors
D39.statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be independent and identically distributed log-concave random vectors taking values in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and let $h$ denote differential entropy. **Folklore conjecture.** The entropy increment $h(X+Y)-h(X)$ is maximized when $X$ and $Y$ have exponential distributions. This conjecture seeks the sharp reverse entropy power inequality in the i.i.d. log-concave setting, where no linear volume-preserving repositioning is needed. Its status is not specified in the source.
